title.zh: 卷三百三十五 列傳第九十四 种世衡子:古 諤 誼 孫:樸 師道 師中
title.en: Volume 335 Biographies 94: Zhong Shiheng and sons: Gu, E, Yi, grandsons: Pu, Shi Dao, Shi Zhong
title.raw: 卷三百三十五 列傳第九十四 种世衡子:古 諤 誼 孫:樸 師道 師中 Volume 335 Biographies 94: Zhong Shiheng and sons: Gu, E, Yi, grandsons: Pu, Shi Dao, Shi Zhong

sentences.zh: 种世衡

translations.literal: Zhong Shiheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shiheng

sentences.zh: 种世衡，字仲平，放之兄子也。

translations.literal: Zhong Shiheng, styled Zhongping, was the nephew of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shiheng, whose courtesy name was Zhongping, was a nephew of Zhong Fang.

sentences.zh: 少尚氣節，昆弟有欲析其貲者，悉推與之，惟取圖書而已。

translations.literal: In youth he prized integrity and resolve; when brothers wished to divide his property, he pushed it all to them and took only books and scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he valued honor and steadfast character. When his brothers wanted to split up the family estate, he gave them everything and kept only his books.

sentences.zh: 以放蔭補將作監主簿，累遷太子中舍。

translations.literal: Through Fang's yin privilege he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and was promoted in succession to Attendant in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through the hereditary privilege owed to Zhong Fang, first as chief clerk in the palace works directorate, and rose step by step to attendant in the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 嘗知涇陽縣，里胥王知謙以姦利事敗，法當徙，遁去。

translations.literal: He once served as magistrate of Jingyang County; the village clerk Wang Zhiqian was exposed in a case of corrupt profit, was liable by law to banishment, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: While magistrate of Jingyang County, he had a village clerk named Wang Zhiqian who was caught in a graft scandal and, facing banishment by law, fled.

sentences.zh: 比郊赦輒出，世衡曰：「送府則會赦」，杖其脊而請罪于府，知府李諮奏釋之。

translations.literal: When suburban amnesty drew near he would emerge; Shiheng said, "If sent to the prefecture he would meet the amnesty," flogged his back, and pleaded guilty at the prefecture; Prefect Li Zi memorialized to release him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang would reappear whenever a suburban amnesty was due. Shiheng said that sending him to the prefectural court would only let him benefit from the pardon, so he had Wang flogged and then presented him to the prefecture to answer for the crime. Prefect Li Zi memorialized for his release.

sentences.zh: 後通判鳳州。

translations.literal: Later he served as deputy prefect of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as deputy prefect of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 州將王蒙正，章獻后姻家也，所為不法。

translations.literal: The prefectural commander Wang Mengzheng was a relative by marriage of Empress Zhangxian and acted unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner of the prefecture, Wang Mengzheng, was connected by marriage to Empress Zhangxian and routinely broke the law.

sentences.zh: 嘗干世衡以私，不聽，蒙正怒，乃誘知謙訟冤而陰助之，世衡坐流竇州，徙汝州。

translations.literal: He once importuned Shiheng for private favor and was not heeded; Mengzheng was angry, then induced Zhiqian to sue for injustice while secretly aiding him, and Shiheng was sentenced to exile in Dou Prefecture and transferred to Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang once tried to pressure Shiheng on a private matter and was refused. Enraged, he egged Wang Zhiqian on to sue for wrongful punishment while secretly backing the suit. Shiheng was banished to Douzhou and then transferred to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟世材上一官以贖，為孟州司馬。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shicai surrendered an office to redeem him and became Defender of Meng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shicai gave up his own post to secure his release and took a post as defender of Mengzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，龍圖閣直學士李紘為辨其誣，宋綬、狄棐繼言之，除衛尉寺丞，歷監隨州酒，簽書同州、鄜州判官事。

translations.literal: After a long time Academician-Expositor of the Dragon Diagram Hall Li Hong cleared his false charge; Song Shou and Di Chai followed in speaking for him; he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Guard Office, successively supervised the wine monopoly of Suizhou, and signed as judicial assistant of Tong and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Li Hong of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion argued that the case had been a frame-up; Song Shou and Di Chai spoke up as well. Shiheng was restored as a vice director in the imperial guard office, later supervised the wine monopoly at Suizhou, and served as signing judicial assistant in Tongzhou and Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 西邊用兵，守備不足。

translations.literal: When war was waged on the western frontier, defenses were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: War on the western frontier had left the border poorly defended.

sentences.zh: 世衡建言，延安東北二百里有故寬州，請因其廢壘而興之，以當寇衝，右可固延安之勢，左可致河東之粟，北可圖銀、夏之舊。

translations.literal: Shiheng submitted a proposal: two hundred li northeast of Yan'an was the old site of Kuan Prefecture; he asked to revive it upon its ruined ramparts to meet the enemy's thrust—on the right it could secure Yan'an's position, on the left draw grain from Hedong, and to the north recover the old territories of Yin and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng proposed rebuilding abandoned Kuanzhou, two hundred li northeast of Yan'an, on its old walls to block the enemy's line of advance. It would shore up Yan'an on one flank, channel grain from Hedong on the other, and open a path toward recovering the former territories of Yin and Xia to the north.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之，命董其役。

translations.literal: The court approved and ordered him to oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and put him in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 夏人屢出爭，世衡且戰且城之。

translations.literal: The Xia people repeatedly came out to contest it; Shiheng fought while building it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tanguts attacked again and again, and Shiheng fought them off even as the walls went up.

sentences.zh: 然處險無泉，議不可守。

translations.literal: Yet the place was perilous and without springs; opinion held it could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: The site was rugged and had no water, and many argued that the fort could not be held.

sentences.zh: 鑿地百五十尺，始至於石，石工辭不可穿，世衡命屑石一畚酬百錢，卒得泉。

translations.literal: They dug one hundred fifty feet before reaching rock; stoneworkers declined that it could not be pierced; Shiheng ordered a basket of stone chips rewarded with a hundred cash, and in the end they obtained a spring.
translations.idiomatic: They dug down a hundred and fifty feet before hitting bedrock. When the masons said the stone could not be broken through, Shiheng offered a hundred cash for every basket of chips removed. They broke through at last and found water.

sentences.zh: 城成，賜名青澗城。

translations.literal: When the city was completed it was granted the name Qingjian Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When the fort was finished, the court named it Qingjian.

sentences.zh: 遷內殿崇班、知城事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inner Hall Esteemed Company and charged with affairs of the fort.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to an inner-hall command post and made administrator of the fort.

sentences.zh: 開營田二千頃，募商賈，貸以本錢，使通貨贏其利，城遂富實。

translations.literal: He opened two thousand qing of garrison farms, recruited merchants, lent them capital, and had them circulate goods to profit, and the fort thereby became wealthy and solid.
translations.idiomatic: He opened two thousand qing of garrison farms, recruited merchants, advanced them capital, and let trade turn a profit until the fort grew prosperous and self-sufficient.

sentences.zh: 間出行部族，慰勞酋長，或解與所服帶。

translations.literal: From time to time he went out among the tribes, comforted the chiefs, and sometimes removed and gave them the belt he wore.
translations.idiomatic: He would tour the tribal districts, console the chiefs, and sometimes take off his own belt and give it to them.

sentences.zh: 嘗會客飲，有得敵情來告者，即以飲器予之，繇是屬羌皆樂為用。

translations.literal: Once while feasting with guests someone came reporting enemy intelligence; he at once gave him his drinking vessel, and from this the dependent Qiang all gladly served him.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast a man brought word of enemy movements. Shiheng immediately gave him his own drinking cup as a reward, and from then on the Qiang under his authority were glad to work for him.

sentences.zh: 再遷洛苑副使、知環州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Luoyuan and made prefect of Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to deputy commissioner of the Luoyuan stud farms and appointed prefect of Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 蕃部有牛家族奴訛者，素屈強，未嘗出謁郡守，聞世衡至，遽郊迎。

translations.literal: Among the tribal peoples was Nue of the Niu family of Bozu, habitually overbearing and strong, who had never gone out to call on the prefect; hearing Shiheng had arrived, he hurried to meet him in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Among the tribes was Nue'er of the Niu clan of Bozu, a man so proud and fierce that he had never come out to greet a prefect. When he heard Shiheng was coming, he rushed to meet him outside the city.

sentences.zh: 世衡與約，明日當至其帳，往勞部落。

translations.literal: Shiheng made an appointment with him that on the morrow he should come to his tent to console the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng promised to visit his camp the next day to pay his respects to the tribe.

sentences.zh: 是夕大雪，深三尺。

translations.literal: That night heavy snow fell, three feet deep.
translations.idiomatic: That night a blizzard piled snow three feet deep.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「地險不可往。」

translations.literal: Those at his side said, "The ground is perilous and one cannot go."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "The terrain is too dangerous—you cannot go."

sentences.zh: 世衡曰：「吾方結諸羌以信，不可失期。」

translations.literal: Shiheng said, "I am just now binding the various Qiang by trust; the appointment cannot be missed."
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng replied, "I am trying to win the Qiang tribes by keeping my word. I cannot break this appointment."

sentences.zh: 遂緣險而進。

translations.literal: He then advanced along the perilous route.
translations.idiomatic: So he pressed on along the treacherous path.

sentences.zh: 奴訛方臥帳中，謂世衡必不能至，世衡蹴而起，奴訛大驚曰：「前此未嘗有官至吾部者，公乃不疑我耶！」

translations.literal: Nue was just then lying in his tent, thinking Shiheng surely could not come; Shiheng kicked and roused him; Nue was greatly startled and said, "Never before has an official reached our tribe—my lord, do you not distrust me!"
translations.idiomatic: Nue'er was still in his tent, sure Shiheng could never make it. Shiheng kicked the tent flap and strode in. Nue'er cried out in astonishment, "No official has ever come to our camp before—yet you trusted me enough to come!"

sentences.zh: 率其族羅拜聽命。

translations.literal: He led his clan in rows to bow and accept orders.
translations.idiomatic: He led his whole clan out to bow in submission.

sentences.zh: 羌酋慕恩部落最強，世衡嘗夜與飲，出侍姬以佐酒。

translations.literal: The Qiang chief Mu'en's tribe was strongest; Shiheng once drank with him at night and produced a serving maid to assist the wine.
translations.idiomatic: Mu'en, the strongest of the Qiang chiefs, once drank with Shiheng late into the night while a concubine poured their wine.

sentences.zh: 既而世衡起入內，潛於壁隙中窺之。

translations.literal: Presently Shiheng rose and went within, secretly peering through a crack in the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng then excused himself, went inside, and watched through a crack in the partition.

sentences.zh: 慕恩竊與侍姬戲，世衡遽出掩之，慕恩慙懼請罪。

translations.literal: Mu'en secretly sported with the serving maid; Shiheng suddenly came out and seized him; Mu'en was ashamed and fearful and begged pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Mu'en began to flirt with the woman. Shiheng burst back in and caught him. Mu'en, ashamed and terrified, begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 世衡笑曰：「君欲之耶？」

translations.literal: Shiheng laughed and said, "My lord desires her?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng laughed and said, "You want her, don't you?"

sentences.zh: 即以遺之，由是得其死力。

translations.literal: He at once gave her to him, and thereby won his utmost loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: He gave her to Mu'en on the spot, and from that day Mu'en would have died for him.

sentences.zh: 諸部有貳者，使討之無不克。

translations.literal: Among the tribes those who were disloyal—when he sent them to punish, none failed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a tribe wavered in loyalty, he sent Mu'en against them and they were always subdued.

sentences.zh: 有兀二族，世衡招之不至，即命慕恩出兵誅之。

translations.literal: There was the Wu'er clan; Shiheng summoned them but they did not come, and he at once ordered Mu'en to take troops and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu'er clan ignored his summons, he sent Mu'en to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 其後百餘帳皆自歸，莫敢貳。

translations.literal: Afterward more than a hundred tents all returned of themselves, none daring disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: After that more than a hundred camps submitted voluntarily, and none dared rebel.

sentences.zh: 因令諸族置烽火，有急則舉燧，介馬以待。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered the various tribes to set beacon fires; when urgent they would raise smoke, with armored horses waiting in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: He then had every tribe maintain beacon fires: at the first alarm they were to light the signal and keep mounted troops ready to ride.

sentences.zh: 葛懷敏敗，率羌兵數千人以振涇原，無敢後者。

translations.literal: When Ge Huaimin was defeated, he led several thousand Qiang troops to succor Jingyuan, none daring to lag behind.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Huaimin's defeat he led several thousand Qiang warriors to reinforce Jingyuan, and not one hung back.

sentences.zh: 嘗課吏民射，有過失，射中則釋其罪；

translations.literal: He once tested officials and commoners in archery; if there was an offense, hitting the target released the crime;
translations.idiomatic: He once held archery trials for officials and commoners alike: if someone had committed an offense, a bull's-eye would win a pardon;

sentences.zh: 有辭某事、請某事，輒因中否而與奪之。

translations.literal: if one pleaded some matter or requested something, he would grant or deny it according to hitting or missing.
translations.idiomatic: and if someone pleaded a case or asked a favor, he granted or denied it according to whether the shot hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 人人自厲，皆精於射，繇是數年敵不敢近環境。

translations.literal: Each person exhorted himself, all became skilled at shooting, and for several years the enemy did not dare approach the borders of Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone drilled himself until the whole district shot superbly. For years afterward the enemy did not dare approach Huanzhou's borders.

sentences.zh: 遷東染院使、環慶路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Institute and Military Controller of Huanqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commissioner of the eastern dyeing institute and military controller of Huanqing circuit.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹檄令與蔣偕築細腰城，世衡時臥病，即起，將所部甲士晝夜興築，城成而卒。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan by dispatch ordered him and Jiang Xie to build Xiyao Fort; Shiheng was then bedridden with illness, but at once rose, led his armored troops day and night in construction, and when the fort was completed he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan ordered him and Jiang Xie to build Xiyao Fort. Shiheng was ill in bed but got up at once, led his troops in round-the-clock construction, and died the day the fort was finished.

sentences.zh: 初，世衡在青澗城，元昊未臣，其貴人野利剛浪㖫、遇乞兄弟有材謀，皆號大王。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shiheng was at Qingjian Fort, Yuan Hao had not yet submitted; his nobles Yeli Ganglangrang and the brothers Yuji were talented in strategy and all were styled Great Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Shiheng held Qingjian, Yuan Hao had not yet submitted to the Song. Yuan's chief advisers, the brothers Yeli Ganglangrang and Yuji, were men of talent and strategy, and each was called a Great King.

sentences.zh: 親信用事，邊臣欲以謀間之。

translations.literal: They were trusted intimates in power, and border officials wished to estrange them by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: They were Yuan's trusted inner circle, and the border officials hoped to drive a wedge between them.

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，鄜延經略使龐籍，兩為保安軍守劉拯書，賂蕃部破醜以達野利兄弟，而涇原路王沿、葛懷敏亦遣人持書及金寶以遣遇乞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingli, Fuyan Frontier Commissioner Pang Ji twice had Bao'an Army defender Liu Zheng write, bribing the tribal people Pochou to reach the Yeli brothers, while Jingyuan Circuit's Wang Yan and Ge Huaimin also sent men bearing letters and gold and jewels to present to Yuji.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli year 2, Pang Ji, commissioner of the Fuyan frontier, twice had Liu Zheng, defender of Bao'an Army, write letters and bribe the tribesman Pochou to reach the Yeli brothers. Wang Yan and Ge Huaimin of Jingyuan circuit also sent envoys with letters and gold and jewels to Yuji.

sentences.zh: 會剛浪㖫令浪埋、賞乞、媚娘等三人詣世衡請降，世衡知其詐，曰：「與其殺之，不若因以為間。」

translations.literal: It happened that Ganglangrang sent Langmai, Shangqi, Meiniang, and three others to Shiheng to request surrender; Shiheng knew it was deceit and said, "Rather than kill them, better use them for estrangement."
translations.idiomatic: Just then Ganglangrang sent three men—Langmai, Shangqi, and Meiniang—to Shiheng offering surrender. Shiheng saw through the ruse and said, "Better to turn them into a wedge than to kill them."

sentences.zh: 留使監商稅，出入騎從甚寵。

translations.literal: He retained them to supervise commercial taxes, and in going out and in they were greatly favored in mounted escort.
translations.idiomatic: He kept them to supervise trade taxes and treated them with conspicuous honor whenever they went abroad.

sentences.zh: 有僧王光信者，趫勇善騎射，習知蕃部山川道路。

translations.literal: There was a monk Wang Guangxin, nimble and brave, skilled in mounted archery, thoroughly knowing the mountains, rivers, and roads of the tribal lands.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Wang Guangxin was swift, brave, and expert with bow and horse, and knew every trail in the tribal country.

sentences.zh: 世衡出兵，常使為鄉導，數蕩族帳，奏以為三班借職，改名嵩。

translations.literal: When Shiheng sent troops he often used him as guide, repeatedly raiding tribal camps; he memorialized appointing him Acting Third Class Attendant and changed his name to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng often used him as guide on campaign and sent him repeatedly against tribal camps. He memorialized for him a third-class attendant post on probation and gave him the name Song.

sentences.zh: 世衡為蠟書，遣嵩遺剛浪㖫，言浪埋等已至，朝廷知王有向漢心，命為夏州節度使，奉錢月萬緡，旌節已至，趣其歸附，以棗綴畫龜，喻其早歸之意。

translations.literal: Shiheng made a wax-sealed letter and sent Song to present it to Ganglangrang, saying Langmai and the others had already arrived, the court knew the king had a heart inclined toward Han, appointed him Military Commissioner of Xia Prefecture with ten thousand strings monthly, insignia of office had arrived, urging his submission, and with jujube strings drew a tortoise to suggest the meaning of early return.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng wrote a secret letter in wax, sent Song to deliver it to Ganglangrang, and claimed that Langmai and the others had already arrived, that the court knew the king favored the Song, that he had been appointed military commissioner of Xia with ten thousand strings of cash each month, and that the imperial commission was already on its way. He urged quick submission and sketched a tortoise with jujube stems to suggest "return soon."

sentences.zh: 剛浪㖫得書大懼，自所治執嵩歸元昊。

translations.literal: Ganglangrang received the letter and was greatly afraid; from his own domain he seized Song and returned him to Yuan Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Ganglangrang was terrified, seized Song in his own territory, and handed him over to Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 元昊疑剛浪㖫貳己，不得還所治，且錮嵩穽中。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao suspected Ganglangrang of disloyalty to himself, would not let him return to his domain, and moreover imprisoned Song in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao suspected Ganglangrang of treachery, refused to let him return to his domain, and threw Song into a dungeon.

sentences.zh: 使其臣李文貴以剛浪㖫旨報世衡，且言不達所遺書意，或許通和，願賜一言。

translations.literal: He sent his minister Li Wengui to report to Shiheng in Ganglangrang's name, and moreover said he did not grasp the meaning of the letter sent, perhaps peace might be allowed, and begged a word be granted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his minister Li Wengui to Shiheng in Ganglangrang's name, saying he had not understood the letter and that peace might be possible if the Song would send a reply.

sentences.zh: 世衡以白籍。

translations.literal: Shiheng reported this to Pang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng reported this to Pang Ji.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷已欲招拊，籍召文貴至，諭以國家寬大開納意，縱使還報。

translations.literal: The court already wished to win them over; Ji summoned Wengui, instructed him in the state's broad and open acceptance, and released him to return with report.
translations.idiomatic: The court was already seeking reconciliation. Pang Ji summoned Wengui, explained the empire's willingness to receive them generously, and sent him back with a reply.

sentences.zh: 元昊得報，出嵩，禮之甚厚，使與文貴偕來。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao received the reply, released Song, treated him with great honor, and had him come together with Wengui.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao received the answer, freed Song, treated him with great honor, and sent him back with Wengui.

sentences.zh: 自是繼遣使者請降，遂稱臣如舊。

translations.literal: From this he successively sent envoys requesting surrender and at last submitted as vassal as before.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys requesting peace followed in succession, and Yuan Hao submitted as a vassal as he had once done.

sentences.zh: 世衡聞野利兄弟已誅，為文越境祭之。

translations.literal: Shiheng heard the Yeli brothers had been executed and composed a text to cross the border and sacrifice to them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiheng learned that the Yeli brothers had been executed, he wrote a memorial text and crossed the border to offer sacrifice for them.

sentences.zh: 籍疏嵩勞，具言元昊未通時，世衡畫策遣嵩冒艱險間其君臣，遂成猜貳，因此與中國通，請優進嵩官。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized to reward Song, fully stating that before Yuan Hao had submitted, Shiheng had devised the plan and sent Song through hardship and peril to estrange ruler and ministers, thereby achieving suspicion and division, and through this communication with China was opened; he requested preferential advancement of Song's office.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji memorialized to reward Song, explaining that before Yuan Hao submitted, Shiheng had plotted to send Song through great danger to sow distrust between ruler and ministers, which had opened the way to peace with the Song, and asked that Song be promoted.

sentences.zh: 遷三班奉職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Third Class Service Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Song was promoted to third-class service attendant.

sentences.zh: 後嵩因對自陳，又進侍禁、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Later Song on audience stated his own case and was further advanced to Palace Attendant Guard and Gatehouse Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Song appeared at court in person, he was advanced again to palace guard attendant and gatehouse attendant.

sentences.zh: 世衡死，籍為樞密使。

translations.literal: When Shiheng died, Ji was Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Shiheng died, Pang Ji became military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 世衡子古上書訟父功，為籍所抑。

translations.literal: Shiheng's son Gu memorialized to sue over his father's merit and was suppressed by Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng's son Gu petitioned to claim credit for his father's service, but Pang Ji blocked it.

sentences.zh: 古復上書，遂贈世衡成州團練使，詔流內銓授古大縣簿尉，押還本貫。

translations.literal: Gu memorialized again, and Shiheng was posthumously granted Regimental Trainer of Cheng Prefecture; an edict ordered the mobile roster to appoint Gu recorder of a large county, and escort him back to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Gu petitioned again. The court posthumously enfeoffed Shiheng as regimental trainer of Chengzhou and ordered the mobile roster to give Gu a recorder post in a large county, then sent him home under escort.

sentences.zh: 籍既罷，古復辯理，下御史考驗，以籍前奏王嵩疏為定。

translations.literal: After Ji was dismissed, Gu again argued the case; it was sent down to the censorate for examination, and Ji's earlier memorial on Wang Song was taken as definitive.
translations.idiomatic: After Pang Ji left office, Gu pressed the case again. The censorate investigated and upheld Pang Ji's earlier memorial about Wang Song.

sentences.zh: 詔以其事付史官，聽古從官便郡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the matter entrusted to the historiographers and permitted Gu to take office in a convenient prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the matter recorded by the historiographers and allowed Gu to take a post wherever he chose.

sentences.zh: 世衡在邊數年，積穀通貨，所至不煩縣官益兵增饋。

translations.literal: Shiheng was on the border several years, amassing grain and circulating goods; wherever he went he did not trouble the district officials to increase troops or add provisions.
translations.idiomatic: During his years on the frontier Shiheng stockpiled grain and kept trade moving, so that wherever he served the court never had to send extra troops or provisions.

sentences.zh: 善撫養士卒，病者遣一子專視其食飲湯劑，以故得人死力。

translations.literal: He was skilled in cherishing troops; for the sick he sent one son solely to attend their food, drink, and medicines, and thereby won men's utmost loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his soldiers well: when a man fell ill he assigned one of his own sons to look after his food and medicine, and so won their absolute loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及卒，羌酋朝夕臨者數日，青澗及環人皆畫象祠之。

translations.literal: When he died, Qiang chiefs attended morning and evening for several days; people of Qingjian and Huan all painted his image and sacrificed to it.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Qiang chiefs came morning and evening for days to mourn him, and people of Qingjian and Huanzhou painted his portrait and set up shrines.

sentences.zh: 子：古、諤、診，皆有將材，關中號曰「三种」。

translations.literal: Sons: Gu, E, Zhen—all had talent as generals; within the passes they were styled "the three Zhongs."
translations.idiomatic: His sons Gu, E, and Zhen all showed generalship, and within the passes they were known as "the three Zhongs."

sentences.zh: 誼，其幼子也。

translations.literal: Yi was his youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was his youngest son.

sentences.zh: 孫：朴、師道、師中。

translations.literal: Grandsons: Pu, Shidao, Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons were Pu, Shidao, and Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 子 古

translations.literal: Son: Gu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Gu

sentences.zh: 古，字大質，少慕從祖放為人，不事科舉。

translations.literal: Gu, styled Dazhi, in youth admired his father's uncle Fang as a man and did not pursue the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, whose courtesy name was Dazhi, admired his grand-uncle Fang from youth and never took the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 當任官，辭以與弟，時稱「小隱君」。

translations.literal: When he was to take office he declined in favor of his younger brother; of the time he was called "the lesser Recluse Lord."
translations.idiomatic: When office was offered him he yielded the post to a younger brother, and people called him "the lesser recluse lord."

sentences.zh: 世衡卒，錄古為天興尉，累轉西京左藏庫副使、涇原路都監、知原州。

translations.literal: When Shiheng died, Gu was recorded as Defender of Tianxing, and was promoted in succession to Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury, Frontier Controller of Jingyuan Circuit, and Prefect of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Shiheng's death Gu was appointed defender of Tianxing and rose through posts as deputy commissioner of the western capital left treasury, frontier controller of Jingyuan circuit, and prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 羌人犯塞，古禦之，斬級數百。

translations.literal: When Qiang people raided the border passes, Gu repelled them and beheaded several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang raiders struck the border, Gu drove them off and took several hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 築城鎮戎之北，以據要害。

translations.literal: He built a fort north of Zhenrong to hold the strategic point.
translations.idiomatic: He built a fort north of Zhenrong to hold a critical pass.

sentences.zh: 神宗召對，遷通事舍人，官其三弟。

translations.literal: Shenzong summoned him for audience, transferred him to Courier Attendant, and enfeoffed his three younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong received him in audience, promoted him to courier attendant, and granted offices to his three younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 與弟診破環州折薑會，斬首二千級，遷西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Zhen he defeated the Zhejiang assembly at Huan Prefecture and beheaded two thousand; he was transferred to Deputy Vice Director of the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He and his brother Zhen defeated the Zhejiang confederation at Huanzhou and took two thousand heads. He was promoted to deputy vice director of the western upper gate.

sentences.zh: 民有損直鬻田於熟羌以避役者，古按其狀，得良田三千頃，丁四千，悉刺為民兵。

translations.literal: Commoners who sold fields below value to settled Qiang to evade corvée—Gu investigated the cases, obtained good fields three thousand qing and four thousand adult males, and all were registered as militia.
translations.idiomatic: Some locals had sold land cheaply to settled Qiang to escape labor duty. Gu investigated, recovered three thousand qing of good farmland and four thousand adult males, and registered them all as militia.

sentences.zh: 歷環慶、永興軍路鈐轄。

translations.literal: He served successively as Military Controller of Huanqing and Yongxingjun circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military controller on Huanqing and Yongxingjun circuits in turn.

sentences.zh: 坐訟范純仁不當，奪一官，知寧州，徙鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: He sat in a case for suing Fan Chunren improperly, was stripped of one office, made prefect of Ning Prefecture, and transferred to Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for improperly suing Fan Chunren, lost one rank, became prefect of Ningzhou, and was transferred to Zhenrong Army.

sentences.zh: 熙河師十萬道境上，須芻糧，僚佐以他路為言。

translations.literal: The Xihe army of one hundred thousand passed the border and needed fodder and grain; subordinates spoke of other routes.
translations.idiomatic: An army of a hundred thousand on the Xihe campaign crossed his territory and needed fodder. His staff urged him to supply another route.

sentences.zh: 古曰：「均王師也。」

translations.literal: Gu said, "All alike are the royal army."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "The imperial army is one body."

sentences.zh: 命給之。

translations.literal: He ordered it supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the supplies delivered.

sentences.zh: 又徙鄜、隰二州，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to the two prefectures Fu and Xi, and died at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Fu and Xizhou and died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 古明達孝義。

translations.literal: Gu was clear-sighted in filial duty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was known for filial piety and moral clarity.

sentences.zh: 弟諤坐擅興繫獄，乞納官贖其罪。

translations.literal: His younger brother E sat in prison for unauthorized action; he begged to surrender office to redeem the crime.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother E was imprisoned for acting without authorization, Gu offered to give up his own post to pay E's penalty.

sentences.zh: 世衡遺張問田千畝，問返之，而世衡死，古終不復受。

translations.literal: Shiheng bequeathed Zhang Wen a thousand mu of fields; Wen returned them, and when Shiheng died Gu in the end never again accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng had left Zhang Wen a grant of a thousand mu. Wen returned it, and after Shiheng's death Gu refused to take it back.

sentences.zh: 然世衡受知於范仲淹，因立青澗功，而古以私憾訟純仁，士論少之。

translations.literal: Yet Shiheng received recognition from Fan Zhongyan and through establishing Qingjian's merit; whereas Gu from private resentment sued Chunren, and scholarly opinion slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet while Shiheng had won Fan Zhongyan's trust and built Qingjian's fame, Gu sued Fan Chunren out of private spite, and educated opinion thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 子 諤

translations.literal: Son: E
translations.idiomatic: Son: E

sentences.zh: 諤，字子正，以父任累官左藏庫副使，延帥陸詵薦知青澗城。

translations.literal: E, styled Zizheng, through his father's appointment accumulated office to Deputy Commissioner of the Left Treasury; Yan'an commander Lu Shen recommended him to know affairs of Qingjian Fort.
translations.idiomatic: E, whose courtesy name was Zizheng, rose through hereditary appointment to deputy commissioner of the left treasury. Lu Shen, commander of Yan'an, recommended him as administrator of Qingjian.

sentences.zh: 夏酋令㖫內附，詵恐生事，欲弗納，諤請納之。

translations.literal: A Xia chief Lingrang came to submit internally; Shen feared trouble and wished not to accept; E requested to accept him.
translations.idiomatic: A Tangut chief named Lingrang offered to submit. Shen feared trouble and wanted to refuse him, but E urged acceptance.

sentences.zh: 夏人來索，詵問所以報，諤曰：「必欲令㖫，當以景詢來易。」

translations.literal: The Xia people came to demand him; Shen asked how to reply; E said, "If they must have Lingrang, they should exchange Jing Xun for him."
translations.idiomatic: When the Tanguts demanded him back, Shen asked how to respond. E said, "If they insist on Lingrang, let them trade us Jing Xun for him."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: They then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That ended the matter.

sentences.zh: 詢者，中國亡命至彼者也。

translations.literal: Xun was a man of China who fled as outlaw to them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xun was a Chinese fugitive who had fled to the Tangut realm.

sentences.zh: 夏將嵬名山部落在故綏州，其弟夷山先降，諤使人因夷山以誘之，賂以金盂，名山小吏李文喜受而許降，而名山未之知也。

translations.literal: The Xia general Wei Mingshan's tribe was at the old Sui Prefecture; his younger brother Yishan had first submitted; E sent men through Yishan to entice him, bribing with a golden bowl; Mingshan's petty clerk Li Wenxi accepted and promised surrender, but Mingshan did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut general Wei Mingshan held the old Suizhou territory. His younger brother Yishan had already submitted, and E used Yishan to lure Mingshan with a golden bowl. Mingshan's clerk Li Wenxi accepted the bribe and promised surrender before Mingshan himself knew.

sentences.zh: 諤即以聞，詔轉運使薛向及陸詵委諤招納。

translations.literal: E at once reported it; an edict ordered Transport Commissioner Xue Xiang and Lu Shen to entrust E with winning them over.
translations.idiomatic: E reported the matter at once. The court ordered transport commissioner Xue Xiang and Lu Shen to put E in charge of the surrender negotiations.

sentences.zh: 諤不待報，悉起所部兵長驅而前，圍其帳。

translations.literal: E did not await reply but raised all his troops in a long drive forward and surrounded his tent.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for approval, E mobilized his entire command, marched straight in, and surrounded Mingshan's camp.

sentences.zh: 名山驚，援槍欲鬪，夷山呼曰：「兄已約降，何為如是？」

translations.literal: Mingshan was startled, seized his spear intending to fight; Yishan cried, "Elder brother has already agreed to surrender—why act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan was startled and seized his spear to fight. Yishan shouted, "Brother, you have already agreed to surrender—why do this?"

sentences.zh: 文喜因出所受金盂示之，名山投槍哭，遂舉眾從諤而南。

translations.literal: Wenxi then produced the golden bowl he had received to show him; Mingshan cast down his spear and wept, and then led all his people to follow E southward.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxi produced the golden bowl he had received. Mingshan dropped his spear and wept, then led his whole tribe south with E.

sentences.zh: 得酋領三百、戶萬五千、兵萬人。

translations.literal: He obtained three hundred chieftains, fifteen thousand households, and ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in three hundred chieftains, fifteen thousand households, and ten thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 將築城，詵以無詔出師，召諤還。

translations.literal: When about to build a fort, Shen because there was no edict for the campaign summoned E back.
translations.idiomatic: As E prepared to build a fort, Shen recalled him on the grounds that he had marched without imperial authorization.

sentences.zh: 軍次懷遠，晨起方櫛，敵四萬眾坌集，傅城而陳。

translations.literal: The army halted at Huaiyuan; at dawn while just combing his hair, the enemy forty thousand in a rush gathered and pressed against the city in array.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Huaiyuan. At dawn, while E was still combing his hair, forty thousand enemy troops surged up and formed battle lines against the walls.

sentences.zh: 諤開門以待，使名山帥新附百餘人挑戰，諤兵繼之，鼓行而出。

translations.literal: E opened the gates to await them, had Mingshan lead more than a hundred of the newly submitted to challenge battle, E's troops followed, and marched out beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: E opened the gates and sent Mingshan with more than a hundred newly submitted warriors to challenge the enemy, then followed with his own troops, advancing to the beat of drums.

sentences.zh: 至晉祠據險，使偏將燕達、劉甫為兩翼，身為中軍，乃閉壘，悉老弱乘城鼓噪以疑賊。

translations.literal: Reaching Jinci he held the perilous ground, set flank generals Yan Da and Liu Fu as two wings, himself as center army, then closed the ramparts and had all old and weak mount the walls beating drums and shouting to confuse the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He took a strong position at Jinci, placed Yan Da and Liu Fu on the wings with himself in the center, then shut the fort and had the old and weak beat drums and shout from the walls to confuse the enemy.

sentences.zh: 已而合戰，追擊二十里，俘馘甚眾，遂城綏州。

translations.literal: Presently they joined battle, pursued twenty li, captured and beheaded very many, and then walled Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They joined battle, pursued the enemy twenty li, took a great number of captives and heads, and then built the walls of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 詵劾諤擅興，且不稟節制，欲捕治，未果而詵徙秦。

translations.literal: Shen impeached E for unauthorized action and for not reporting to command, wished to arrest and punish him, but did not succeed before Shen was transferred to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Shen impeached E for acting without authorization and ignoring command, and tried to have him arrested, but failed before Shen himself was transferred to Qin.

sentences.zh: 言者交攻之，遂下吏，貶秩四等，安置隨州。

translations.literal: Memorialists attacked him in succession; he was sent down to the clerks, demoted four ranks, and settled at Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics piled on, and E was handed over to the courts, demoted four ranks, and exiled to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 會侯可以言水利入見，神宗問其事，對曰：「种諤奉密旨取綏而獲罪，後何以使人？」

translations.literal: It happened that Hou Ke, who spoke on waterworks, entered audience; Shenzong asked about the matter; he replied, "Zhong E received secret orders to take Sui yet was punished—how afterward can one employ men?"
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ke, an expert on waterworks, happened to appear at court. When Shenzong asked about the case, he said, "Zhong E carried out a secret order to recover Suizhou and was punished for it—who will dare serve the throne after this?"

sentences.zh: 帝亦悔，復其官。

translations.literal: The emperor also regretted it and restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted the affair and restored E's rank.

sentences.zh: 韓絳宣撫陝西，用為鄜延鈐轄。

translations.literal: Han Jiang was Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi and employed him as Fuyan Military Controller.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang became pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, he appointed E military controller of Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 絳城囉兀，規橫山，令諤將兵二萬出無定川，命諸將皆受節度，起河東兵會銀州。

translations.literal: Jiang walled Luo'er, planned Hengshan, ordered E to lead twenty thousand troops out the Wuding River valley, commanded all generals to accept his direction, and raised Hedong troops to join at Yin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han walled Luo'er and planned an advance on Hengshan. He ordered E to lead twenty thousand men down the Wuding River, placed all generals under his command, and raised Hedong troops to rendezvous at Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 城成而慶卒叛，詔罷師，棄囉兀，責授汝州團練副使。

translations.literal: When the fort was completed the Qingzhou troops rebelled; an edict halted the army, abandoned Luo'er, and demoted him to Deputy Regimental Trainer of Ru Prefecture by way of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The fort was finished just as Qingzhou troops mutinied. The court ordered the campaign halted, abandoned Luo'er, and demoted E to deputy regimental trainer of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 再貶賀州別駕，移單州，又移華州。

translations.literal: He was again demoted to Vice Prefect of He Prefecture, transferred to Shan Prefecture, and again to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again to vice prefect of Hezhou, then transferred to Shanzhou and later to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 絳再相，訟其前功，復禮賓副使、知岷州。

translations.literal: When Jiang was again chief minister he sued for his former merit; he was restored as Deputy Commissioner of Ceremonial Guests and made prefect of Min Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang returned as chief minister, he pleaded E's earlier service. E was restored as deputy commissioner of ceremonial guests and made prefect of Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 董氈將鬼章聚兵於洮、岷，新羌多叛，諤討襲誅之。

translations.literal: Dong Zhan and Guizhang gathered troops at Tao and Min; many new Qiang rebelled; E attacked in raids and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhan and Guizhang raised troops on the Tao and Min rivers, and many newly submitted Qiang rebelled. E raided them and put the ringleaders to death.

sentences.zh: 從李憲出塞，收洮州，下逋宗、講珠、東宜諸城，掩擊至大河，斬首七千級。

translations.literal: Following Li Xian beyond the passes, he recovered Tao Prefecture, took the cities Tongzong, Jiangzhu, Dongyi, and others, made a surprise attack to the Great River, and beheaded seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Following Li Xian beyond the border, he recovered Taozhou, captured Tongzong, Jiangzhu, Dongyi, and other towns, and struck in a surprise raid to the Great River, taking seven thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 遷東上閤門使、文州刺史、知涇州，徙鄜延副總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Eastern Upper Gate Vice Director, Prefect of Wen Prefecture, and Administrator of Jing Prefecture, and moved to Deputy Commander of Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to eastern upper gate vice director and prefect of Wenzhou, made administrator of Jingzhou, and transferred to deputy commander of Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 上言：「夏主秉常為其母所囚，可急因本路官搗其巢穴。」

translations.literal: He submitted: "The Xia ruler Bingchang is imprisoned by his mother; one may urgently use officials of this circuit to strike their nest."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The Tangut ruler Bingchang is held prisoner by his mother. We should strike their heartland at once through the officials of this circuit."

sentences.zh: 遂入對，大言曰：「夏國無人，秉常孺子，臣往持其臂以來耳。」

translations.literal: He then entered audience and spoke boldly: "The Xia state has no men; Bingchang is a child—your servant will go and lead him by the arm to come."
translations.idiomatic: At court he boasted: "The Tanguts have no real leaders—Bingchang is only a boy. I will go and lead him here by the arm."

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，決意西討，以為經略安撫副使，諸將悉聽節制。

translations.literal: The emperor was heartened, resolved on western campaign, made him Frontier Pacification Deputy Commissioner, and all generals were to heed his direction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stirred and resolved on a western campaign. He made E frontier pacification deputy commissioner, with all generals under his command.

sentences.zh: 諤即次境上，帝以諤先期輕出，使聽令于王中正。

translations.literal: E at once encamped on the border; the emperor because E had gone out lightly ahead of time made him obey Wang Zhongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: E encamped on the frontier, but because he had moved out too boldly the emperor placed him under Wang Zhongzheng's orders.

sentences.zh: 敵屯兵夏州，諤率本路並畿內七將兵攻米脂，三日未下。

translations.literal: The enemy encamped at Xia Prefecture; E led this circuit's and the capital district's seven generals' troops to attack Mizhi, three days without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held Xiazhou. E led the seven generals of his circuit and the capital district against Mizhi, but failed to take it in three days.

sentences.zh: 夏兵八萬來援，諤禦之無定川，伏兵發，斷其首尾，大破之，降守將令介訛遇。

translations.literal: Eighty thousand Xia troops came to aid; E met them on the Wuding River, ambush troops sprang up, cut their head and tail, routed them greatly, and the defending general Lingjierangyu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty thousand Tangut reinforcements arrived. E met them on the Wuding River, sprang an ambush that cut their column in two, routed them completely, and accepted the surrender of the defender Lingjierangyu.

sentences.zh: 捷書聞，帝大喜，群臣稱賀，遣中使諭獎，而罷中正。

translations.literal: Victory report was heard; the emperor was greatly pleased, the courtiers congratulated, sent palace envoy to instruct and reward, and dismissed Zhongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the emperor rejoiced, the court congratulated him, and a palace envoy was sent with rewards while Wang Zhongzheng was removed from command.

sentences.zh: 諤留千人守米脂，進次銀、石、夏州，不見敵。

translations.literal: E left a thousand to guard Mizhi and advanced to station at Yin, Shi, and Xia prefectures, not seeing the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: E left a thousand men at Mizhi and advanced through Yin, Shi, and Xiazhou without meeting resistance.

sentences.zh: 始，被詔當會靈武，諤迂枉不進，士卒饑憊，欲以糧運不繼歸罪轉運使李稷。

translations.literal: At first, having received orders to join at Lingwu, E took a circuitous route and did not advance; troops were hungry and weary; he wished to lay blame on Transport Commissioner Li Ji for interrupted grain supply.
translations.idiomatic: He had been ordered to rendezvous at Lingwu but took a roundabout route and stalled. His troops grew hungry and exhausted, and he planned to blame transport commissioner Li Ji for the broken supply line.

sentences.zh: 駐軍麻家平，大校劉歸仁以眾潰，詔令班師。

translations.literal: He encamped at Majiaping; Senior Commander Liu Guiren's troops collapsed in flight; an edict ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Majiaping, where senior commander Liu Guiren's troops broke and fled. The court ordered a full withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 猶遷鳳州團練使、龍神衛四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was still transferred to Regimental Trainer of Feng Prefecture and Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was still promoted to regimental trainer of Fengzhou and commander of the four wings of the Dragon Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 諤謀據橫山之志未已，遣子朴上其策。

translations.literal: E's design to hold Hengshan was not yet ended; he sent his son Pu to present the plan.
translations.idiomatic: E still meant to seize Hengshan and sent his son Pu to present the plan at court.

sentences.zh: 帝召朴問狀，擢為閤門祗候。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Pu to question the plan and promoted him to Gatehouse Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Pu in person and promoted him to gatehouse attendant.

sentences.zh: 將進城橫山，命徐禧、李舜舉使鄜延計議。

translations.literal: About to advance and wall Hengshan, he ordered Xu Xi and Li Shunju to go to Fuyan to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared to fortify Hengshan, it sent Xu Xi and Li Shunju to Fuyan to consult with E.

sentences.zh: 諤言：「橫山延袤千里，多馬宜稼，人物勁悍善戰，且有鹽鐵之利，夏人恃以為生；

translations.literal: E said: "Hengshan extends a thousand li, has many horses and suits grain, its people are strong and fierce and skilled in battle, and moreover has the profit of salt and iron—the Xia people rely on it for livelihood;
translations.idiomatic: E argued: "Hengshan stretches a thousand li. Its pastures and fields are rich, its people fierce and warlike, and it holds salt and iron—the Tanguts depend on it for their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 其城壘皆控險，足以守禦。

translations.literal: its forts and ramparts all hold perilous ground, sufficient to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Its forts all sit on commanding ground and are easy to defend.

sentences.zh: 今之興功，當自銀州始。

translations.literal: For present works one should begin from Yin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Our work should begin at Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 其次遷宥州，又其次修夏州，三郡鼎峙，則橫山之地已囊括其中。

translations.literal: Next relocate You Prefecture, next again repair Xia Prefecture—three prefectures like a tripod, then Hengshan's lands are already embraced within.
translations.idiomatic: Next move Youzhou, then rebuild Xiazhou. Once those three posts stand like a tripod, Hengshan will be enclosed.

sentences.zh: 又其次修鹽州，則橫山強兵戰馬、山澤之利，盡歸中國。

translations.literal: Next again repair Yan Prefecture, then Hengshan's strong troops, war horses, and mountain marsh profits all return to China.
translations.idiomatic: Then fortify Yanzhou, and Hengshan's soldiers, horses, and mountain resources will all belong to the Song.

sentences.zh: 其勢居高，俯視興、靈，可以直覆巢穴。」

translations.literal: Its position is high and overlooks Xing and Ling; one can directly overturn their nest."
translations.idiomatic: From that height we would look down on Xing and Ling and strike straight at their heartland."

sentences.zh: 而禧與沈括定議移銀州，城永樂，與諤始謀異，乃奏留諤守延。

translations.literal: But Xi and Shen Kuo fixed the plan to move Yin Prefecture and wall Yongle, differing from E's original plan, and memorialized to keep E guarding Yan.
translations.idiomatic: But Xu Xi and Shen Kuo decided to relocate Yinzhou and build Yongle instead. Their plan differed from E's, and they memorialized to keep him on the Yan'an frontier.

sentences.zh: 既而永樂受圍，諤觀望不救，帝冀其後效，置不問，且虞賊至，就命知延州。

translations.literal: Presently Yongle was besieged; E watched and did not rescue; the emperor hoped for later merit and set it aside; moreover fearing the enemy would come, he was at once appointed to know Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongle was besieged, E held back and did not relieve it. The emperor still hoped for better service from him and said nothing, then appointed him prefect of Yanzhou for fear of an enemy attack.

sentences.zh: 疽發背卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: A carbuncle broke out on his back and he died at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: A carbuncle on his back killed him at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 諤善馭士卒，臨敵出奇，戰必勝，然詐誕殘忍，左右有犯立斬，或先刳肺肝，坐者掩面，諤飲食自若。

translations.literal: E was skilled in controlling troops, in facing the enemy produced the unexpected, in battle always won; yet he was deceitful, boastful, and cruel—if those at his side offended he beheaded them at once, sometimes first cutting open lungs and liver; those seated covered their faces, while E ate and drank as usual.
translations.idiomatic: E commanded soldiers superbly, fought with daring stratagems, and never lost a battle, yet he was cunning, boastful, and cruel. Anyone who offended him was beheaded on the spot, sometimes after his lungs and liver were cut out first. Guests covered their faces while E ate and drank as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 敵亦畏其敢戰，故數有功。

translations.literal: The enemy also feared his readiness to fight, and therefore he repeatedly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy feared his willingness to fight, which is why he won so often.

sentences.zh: 李稷之饋軍也，旦入諤營，軍吏鳴鼓聲喏。

translations.literal: When Li Ji came to supply the army, at dawn he entered E's camp; military clerks beat drums and shouted salute.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ji came at dawn to deliver supplies to E's camp, the camp clerks beat drums and shouted formal salutes.

sentences.zh: 諤呼問吏曰：「軍有幾帥？

translations.literal: E called and asked the clerk, "How many commanders does the army have?
translations.idiomatic: E called out, "How many commanders does this army have?

sentences.zh: 要當借汝頭以代運使。」

translations.literal: I must borrow your head to replace the transport commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: I need your head to take the transport commissioner's place."

sentences.zh: 即叱斬之。

translations.literal: He at once shouted and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 稷惶怖遽出。

translations.literal: Ji in terror and fear hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji fled the camp in terror.

sentences.zh: 嘗渡河，猝遇敵，紿門下客曰：「事急矣，可衣我衣，乘我馬，從旗鼓千騎，亟趨大軍。」

translations.literal: Once crossing a river he suddenly met the enemy; he deceived a client at his gate saying, "The matter is urgent—you may wear my robe, ride my horse, follow the banners and drums with a thousand riders, and hasten to the great army."
translations.idiomatic: Once while crossing a river he suddenly met the enemy. He told a client, "This is urgent—put on my robe, take my horse, ride out with a thousand men under my banners, and hurry to the main force."

sentences.zh: 客信之，敵以為諤，追之，幾不免。

translations.literal: The client believed him; the enemy thought it was E and pursued; he nearly did not escape.
translations.idiomatic: The man believed him. The enemy took him for E and pursued him hard, while E himself barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧首開綏州，後再舉西征，皆其兆謀，卒致永樂之禍。

translations.literal: From Xining's first opening of Sui Prefecture, afterward twice raising western campaigns—all were his initiating plans, and in the end brought the disaster of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: From the first recovery of Suizhou in the Xining era through the later western campaigns, the plans were largely his, and they ended in the Yongle disaster.

sentences.zh: 議者謂諤不死，邊事不已。

translations.literal: Critics said if E had not died, border affairs would not have ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said that if E had lived, the border wars would never have ended.

sentences.zh: 子 誼

translations.literal: Son: Yi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yi

sentences.zh: 誼，字壽翁。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Shouweng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose courtesy name was Shouweng.

sentences.zh: 熙甯中，古入對，神宗問其家世，命誼以官。

translations.literal: In the Xining era Gu entered audience; Shenzong asked his family background and ordered Yi given office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era, when Gu appeared at court, Shenzong asked about the family and granted Yi an office.

sentences.zh: 從高遵裕復洮、岷，又平山後羌，至熙河副將。

translations.literal: Following Gao Zunyu he recovered Tao and Min, again pacified the Shanhou Qiang, and reached Deputy General of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Zunyu in recovering Tao and Min, pacified the Qiang beyond the mountains, and rose to deputy general on the Xihe front.

sentences.zh: 使青唐，董氈遣鬼章迎候境上，取道故為回枉，以誇險遠。

translations.literal: Sent to Qingtang, Dong Zhan dispatched Guizhang to welcome him at the border; he deliberately took a roundabout route to boast of peril and distance.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Qingtang, Dong Zhan sent Guizhang to meet him at the border. Guizhang deliberately took a roundabout route to impress Yi with the land's remoteness and danger.

sentences.zh: 誼固習其地里，誚之曰：「爾跳梁坎井間，謂我不知遠近邪？」

translations.literal: Yi was well versed in its terrain; he mocked him saying, "You leap about between pit and well—do you think I do not know near and far?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi knew the country well and mocked him: "You strut in your own little corner and think I cannot tell distance?"

sentences.zh: 命趨便道。

translations.literal: He ordered him to take the convenient route.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them onto the direct road.

sentences.zh: 鬼章怒，脅以兵，誼聲氣不動，卒改塗。

translations.literal: Guizhang was angry and threatened with troops; Yi's voice and bearing did not move; in the end they changed route.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhang grew angry and threatened him with troops, but Yi never flinched, and they finally changed course.

sentences.zh: 外為路都監。

translations.literal: Externally he was Circuit Frontier Controller.
translations.idiomatic: He served as frontier controller of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 自蘭州渡河討賊，斬首六百，累轉西京使。

translations.literal: From Lan Prefecture he crossed the river to punish bandits, beheaded six hundred, and was promoted in succession to Western Capital Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river from Lanzhou to attack rebels, he took six hundred heads and was promoted to western capital commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，知岷州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was made prefect of Min Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era he became prefect of Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 鬼章誘殺景思立，後益自矜，大有窺故土之心，使其子詣宗哥請益兵入寇，且結屬羌為內應。

translations.literal: Guizhang lured and killed Jing Sili; afterward he grew more arrogant, greatly harbored designs on old territory, sent his son to Zongge to request added troops for invasion, and moreover joined dependent Qiang as internal response.
translations.idiomatic: After Guizhang lured and killed Jing Sili, he grew arrogant and began plotting to recover his old lands. He sent his son to Zongge to ask for reinforcements and win dependent Qiang tribes as inside allies.

sentences.zh: 誼刺得其情，上疏請除之。

translations.literal: Yi spied out the facts and memorialized requesting his removal.
translations.idiomatic: Yi uncovered the plot and memorialized for permission to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 詔遣游師雄就商利害，遂與姚兕合兵出討。

translations.literal: An edict sent You Shixiong to consult on advantage and harm; he then joined Yao Ni in combined troops to campaign and punish.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent You Shixiong to weigh the plan, and Yi joined Yao Ni in a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 羌迎戰，擊走之，追奔至洮州。

translations.literal: The Qiang met them in battle; they struck and drove them off, pursuing in flight to Tao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang met them in battle and were driven back all the way to Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 誼亟進攻，晨霧蔽野，跬步不可辨。

translations.literal: Yi urgently pressed the attack; morning fog covered the wilds, and a single step could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Yi pressed the attack at once, but morning fog covered the field so thickly that one could not see a step ahead.

sentences.zh: 誼曰：「吾軍遠來，彼固不知厚薄，乘此可一鼓而下也。」

translations.literal: Yi said, "Our army has come from afar; they surely do not know our strength and weakness—seizing this we can take them in one drumbeat."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "We have come from far away, and they cannot yet judge our strength. We should take the city in a single assault."

sentences.zh: 遂親鼓之。

translations.literal: He then personally beat the drums.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the drums himself.

sentences.zh: 有頃，霧霽，先登者已得城，鬼章就執。

translations.literal: After a while the fog cleared; those who first mounted already had the city; Guizhang was then seized.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the fog lifted. The first men over the wall had already taken the city, and Guizhang was captured.

sentences.zh: 誼戲問之曰：「別後安否？」

translations.literal: Yi in jest asked him, "Since we parted, are you well?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked jokingly, "Have you been well since we last met?"

sentences.zh: 不能對，徐謂人曰：「我生惡种使，今日果為所擒。

translations.literal: He could not reply; slowly he told others, "I have hated the Zhong envoy all my life—today I am indeed seized by him.
translations.idiomatic: He could not answer, then said slowly to those around him, "I have hated the Zhong envoy all my life, and today he has caught me.

sentences.zh: 天不使我復有故土，命也。」

translations.literal: Heaven does not let me again have old territory—it is fate."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven will not let me recover my old lands. It is fate."

sentences.zh: 遂俘以歸。

translations.literal: He was then taken captive and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took him back as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 拜西上閤門使、康州刺史，徙知鄜州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Western Upper Gate Vice Director and Prefect of Kang Prefecture, and transferred to know Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made western upper gate vice director and prefect of Kangzhou, then transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏人犯延安，趙禼使誼統諸將。

translations.literal: The Xia people raided Yan'an; Zhao Xu had Yi command all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tanguts attacked Yan'an, Zhao Xu put Yi in command of all the generals.

sentences.zh: 敵聞誼至，皆潰去。

translations.literal: The enemy hearing Yi had come all collapsed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy heard Yi had arrived, they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 延人謂：「得誼，勝精兵二十萬。」

translations.literal: People of Yan said, "To obtain Yi surpasses two hundred thousand elite troops."
translations.idiomatic: People in Yan'an said, "Getting Yi is worth two hundred thousand elite troops."

sentences.zh: 進熙河鈐轄、知蘭州。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Xihe Military Controller and made to know Lan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military controller of Xihe and prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 蘭與通遠皆絕塞，中間保障不相接，腴田多棄不耕，誼請城李諾平以扼衝要。

translations.literal: Lan and Tongyuan were both remote passes; between them protective posts did not connect, fertile fields were mostly abandoned uncultivated; Yi requested to wall Linuoping to choke the strategic point.
translations.idiomatic: Lanzhou and Tongyuan were isolated frontier posts with no connecting defenses between them, and rich farmland lay fallow. Yi asked to build a fort at Linuoping to hold a critical pass.

sentences.zh: 會遷東上閤門使、保州團練使，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: It happened that he was transferred to Eastern Upper Gate Vice Director and Regimental Trainer of Bao Prefecture; he died at age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to eastern upper gate vice director and regimental trainer of Baozhou, but died at fifty-five before the fort could be built.

sentences.zh: 誼倜儻有氣節，喜讀書。

translations.literal: Yi was free-spirited with integrity and resolve, and delighted in reading books.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was bold and high-minded, with a love of books.

sentences.zh: 蒞軍整嚴，令一下，死不敢避；

translations.literal: When he arrived the army was sternly ordered; once an order issued, none dared avoid death;
translations.idiomatic: He ran his commands with iron discipline: once an order was given, men faced death without flinching;

sentences.zh: 遇敵，度不勝不出，故每戰未嘗負敗。

translations.literal: meeting the enemy, if he judged he could not win he did not go out, and therefore in every battle he never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: and he never offered battle unless he was sure of victory, so he was never defeated.

sentences.zh: 岷羌酋包順、包誠恃功驕恣，前守務姑息，誼至，厚待之。

translations.literal: The Min Qiang chiefs Bao Shun and Bao Cheng relied on merit and were arrogant and unrestrained; former administrators all sought indulgence; when Yi arrived he treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Minzhou Qiang chiefs Bao Shun and Bao Cheng had grown arrogant on their past service, and earlier prefects had indulged them. Yi treated them generously at first.

sentences.zh: 適有小過，叱下吏，將置法，順、誠叩頭伏罪，願效命以贖，乃使輸金出之，群羌畏惕。

translations.literal: When they had a small offense he shouted them down to the clerks and was about to apply the law; Shun and Cheng knocked their heads and confessed guilt, wished to serve with their lives to redeem it; he then had them pay gold to release them, and all the Qiang were in fear and caution.
translations.idiomatic: When they committed a minor offense he hauled them before the clerks to be punished. They kowtowed and begged to redeem themselves with service. He fined them in gold and let them go, and the Qiang tribes were cowed.

sentences.zh: 及洮州之役，二人功最多。

translations.literal: At the Tao Prefecture campaign the two men's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: At the Taozhou campaign they did the greatest service.

sentences.zh: 孫 朴

translations.literal: Grandson: Pu
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Pu

sentences.zh: 朴以父任右班殿直，積勞，遷至皇城使、昌州刺史，徙熙河蘭會鈐轄兼知河州，安撫洮西沿邊公事。

translations.literal: Pu through his father's appointment was Right Company Attendant of the Hall, accumulated merit, was transferred to Imperial City Commissioner and Prefect of Chang Prefecture, moved to Xihe Lan-Hui Military Controller while also knowing He Prefecture, pacifying affairs along the Tao western border.
translations.idiomatic: Pu entered service through his father's privilege as a right company attendant, rose through merit to imperial city commissioner and prefect of Changzhou, then became military controller of Lan and Hui on the Xihe front while also governing Hezhou and overseeing border affairs west of the Tao River.

sentences.zh: 河南蕃部叛，屬羌阿章率他族拒官軍，熙帥胡宗回使朴出討。

translations.literal: The Henan tribal peoples rebelled; dependent Qiang Azhan led other clans to resist the official army; Xihe commander Hu Zonghui had Pu go out to punish.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes south of the river rebelled, and the dependent Qiang leader Azhan rallied other clans against the government army. The Xihe commander Hu Zonghui sent Pu to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 時朴至州才二日，以賊鋒方銳，且盛寒，欲姑徐之，而宗回馳檄至六七，不得已，遂出兵。

translations.literal: At the time Pu had reached the prefecture only two days; because the bandits' edge was just sharp and moreover it was bitter cold, he wished for the moment to delay; but Zonghui's urgent dispatches came six or seven times, and having no choice he then sent out troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pu had been in the prefecture only two days. The rebels were at their peak and the weather was bitterly cold, so he wanted to wait, but Zonghui sent six or seven urgent dispatches. He had no choice but to march out.

sentences.zh: 羌知朴來，伏以待。

translations.literal: The Qiang knew Pu was coming and lay in ambush to await him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang knew he was coming and set an ambush.

sentences.zh: 朴遇伏，首尾不相應，朴殊死戰，為賊所殺，以馬負其屍去。

translations.literal: Pu met the ambush; head and tail did not respond to each other; Pu fought desperately to the death, was killed by bandits, and they carried off his corpse on a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Pu walked into the trap. His van and rear could not coordinate. He fought to the death and was killed, and the enemy carried off his body on horseback.

sentences.zh: 羌乘勝追北。

translations.literal: The Qiang pursued northward on the momentum of victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang pursued the retreating army in victory.

sentences.zh: 師還遇隘，壅迮不得行。

translations.literal: The army on returning met a narrow pass, choked and jammed and unable to advance.
translations.idiomatic: On the retreat they hit a narrow pass and could not get through.

sentences.zh: 偏將王舜臣者善射，以弓卦臂，獨立敗軍後。

translations.literal: Flank general Wang Shunchen was skilled at archery; with bow slung on arm he stood alone behind the defeated army.
translations.idiomatic: Flank general Wang Shunchen was a superb archer. With his bow on his arm he stood alone at the rear of the broken column.

sentences.zh: 羌來可萬騎，有七人介馬而先。

translations.literal: The Qiang came in perhaps ten thousand riders; seven men in armor on horses went ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten thousand Qiang horsemen came up, with seven armored riders in the lead.

sentences.zh: 舜臣念此必羌酋之尤桀黠者，不先殪之，吾軍必盡。

translations.literal: Shunchen thought these must be the most fierce and cunning of Qiang chiefs; if not first killed, his army would be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Shunchen reckoned these must be the boldest Qiang chiefs. Unless he killed them first, his army would be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 乃宣言曰：「吾令最先行者眉間插花。」

translations.literal: He then proclaimed, "I decree that those who go foremost shall wear flowers between the brows."
translations.idiomatic: He called out, "I will put a flower between the brows of whoever rides in front."

sentences.zh: 引弓三發，隕三人，皆中面；

translations.literal: He drew the bow and shot three times; three fell, all struck in the face;
translations.idiomatic: He loosed three arrows and dropped three men, each shot in the face;

sentences.zh: 餘四人反走，矢貫其背。

translations.literal: the remaining four turned and fled, arrows piercing their backs.
translations.idiomatic: the other four wheeled about and fled with arrows through their backs.

sentences.zh: 萬騎𥈭眙莫敢前，舜臣因得整眾。

translations.literal: The ten thousand riders stared in shock and dared not advance; Shunchen thereby was able to reorganize the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The ten thousand horsemen stared in shock and dared not advance, and Shunchen was able to rally his men.

sentences.zh: 須臾，羌復來。

translations.literal: After a moment the Qiang came again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Qiang attacked again.

sentences.zh: 舜臣自申及酉，抽矢千餘發，無虛者。

translations.literal: From the shen hour to the you hour Shunchen drew more than a thousand arrows, none in vain.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-afternoon until evening he shot more than a thousand arrows without a miss.

sentences.zh: 指裂，血流至肘。

translations.literal: His fingers split open, blood flowing to the elbows.
translations.idiomatic: His fingers split open and blood ran to his elbows.

sentences.zh: 薄暮，乃得逾隘。

translations.literal: At dusk he was able to cross the pass.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the army finally got through the pass.

sentences.zh: 將士氣奪，無敢復言戰。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers had their spirit seized; none dared speak again of battle.
translations.idiomatic: The troops' spirit was broken, and no one dared speak of fighting again.

sentences.zh: 當是時，微舜臣則師殲矣。

translations.literal: At that time, but for Shunchen the army would have been annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Without Shunchen the whole force would have been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈朴雄州防禦使，官其後十人。

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, Pu was posthumously granted Defender of Xiong Prefecture, and ten of his descendants were given office.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Pu was posthumously made defender of Xiongzhou, and ten of his descendants were granted offices.

sentences.zh: 孫 師道

translations.literal: Grandson: Shidao
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Shidao

sentences.zh: 師道，字彝叔。

translations.literal: Shidao, styled Yishu.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao, whose courtesy name was Yishu.

sentences.zh: 少從張載學，以蔭補三班奉職，試法，易文階，為熙州推官、權同谷縣。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Zhang Zai; through yin privilege he was appointed Third Class Service Attendant, passed the law examination, changed to civil rank, and became Judicial Officer of Xi Prefecture and Acting Magistrate of Tonggu County.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Zhang Zai in youth, entered office through hereditary privilege as a third-class service attendant, passed the law examination, shifted to civil rank, and served as judicial officer of Xizhou and acting magistrate of Tonggu.

sentences.zh: 縣吏有田訟，彌二年不決。

translations.literal: A county clerk had a land lawsuit that for two full years was not decided.
translations.idiomatic: A county clerk had a land dispute that had dragged on unresolved for two years.

sentences.zh: 師道繙閱案牘，窮日力不竟，然所訟止母及兄而已。

translations.literal: Shidao turned through the case documents, exhausting the day's strength without finishing, yet what was sued over was only mother and elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao pored over the case files all day without finishing, yet the suit involved only the clerk's mother and elder brother.

sentences.zh: 引吏詰之曰：「母、兄，法可訟乎。

translations.literal: He summoned the clerk and interrogated him: "Mother and elder brother—may one sue them by law?
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the clerk and demanded, "Your mother and brother—does the law allow you to sue them?

sentences.zh: 汝再期擾鄉里足未？」

translations.literal: Have you not had enough of troubling the village for two terms?"
translations.idiomatic: Haven't you troubled the district long enough?"

sentences.zh: 吏叩頭服罪。

translations.literal: The clerk knocked his head and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk kowtowed and confessed.

sentences.zh: 通判原州，提舉秦鳳常平。

translations.literal: He served as deputy prefect of Yuan Prefecture and promoted the Qinfeng Ever-Normal Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy prefect of Yuanzhou and as promoter of the Qinfeng ever-normal granary.

sentences.zh: 議役法忤蔡京旨，換莊宅使、知德順軍。

translations.literal: In discussing the labor-service law he offended Cai Jing's intent; he was transferred to Estate Commissioner and made to know Deshun Army.
translations.idiomatic: His criticism of the labor-service law offended Cai Jing. He was transferred to estate commissioner and made commander of Deshun Army.

sentences.zh: 又謂其詆毀先烈，罷入黨籍，屏廢十年。

translations.literal: He was again said to have slandered former worthies, dismissed into the faction register, and set aside for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He was also accused of slandering former worthies, struck from office, enrolled among the proscribed faction, and banished from public life for ten years.

sentences.zh: 以武功大夫、忠州刺史、涇原都鈐轄知懷德軍。

translations.literal: As Martial Merit Grandee, Prefect of Zhong Prefecture, and Jingyuan Frontier Controller he knew affairs of Huaide Army.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as martial merit grandee, prefect of Zhongzhou, frontier controller of Jingyuan, and commander of Huaide Army.

sentences.zh: 夏國畫境，其人焦彥堅必欲得故地，師道曰：「如言故地，當以漢、唐為正，則君家疆土益蹙矣。」

translations.literal: The Xia state demarcated the border; their man Jiao Yanjian insisted on obtaining old territory; Shidao said, "If one speaks of old territory, taking Han and Tang as standard, then your state's lands would shrink all the more."
translations.idiomatic: When the Tanguts demarcated the border, their envoy Jiao Yanjian insisted on recovering old lands. Shidao said, "If we take Han and Tang as the standard for 'old lands,' your realm would shrink even further."

sentences.zh: 彥賢無以對。

translations.literal: Yanxian had nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxian had no answer.

sentences.zh: 童貫握兵柄而西，翕張威福，見者皆旅拜，師道長揖而已。

translations.literal: Tong Guan grasped military power and went west, expanding and contracting authority and favor; those who saw him all bowed in rows; Shidao only made a long bow.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan took military command in the west and threw his weight about, everyone bowed low before him. Shidao gave only a formal bow.

sentences.zh: 召詣闕，徽宗訪以邊事，對曰：「先為不可勝，來則應之。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the court; Huizong inquired about border affairs; he replied, "First make oneself unconquerable; when they come, respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he told Huizong on border affairs, "Make yourself unbeatable first, then respond when the enemy comes.

sentences.zh: 妄動生事，非計也。」

translations.literal: Rash movement and creating incidents is not a plan."
translations.idiomatic: Rash action is no strategy."

sentences.zh: 貫議徙內郡弓箭手實邊，而指為新邊所募。

translations.literal: Guan planned to move archer militia of inner prefectures to fill the border, but represented them as newly recruited on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Guan planned to shift archer militia from inner prefectures to the frontier but presented them as newly recruited border troops.

sentences.zh: 帝復訪之，對曰：「臣恐勤遠之功未立，而近擾先及矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor again questioned him; he replied, "Your servant fears that merit in toiling for distant goals is not yet established, while nearby disturbance will first arrive."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him again. He said, "I fear the court will trouble the near provinces before any distant campaign succeeds."

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，賜襲衣、金帶，以為提舉秦鳳弓箭手。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words, bestowed court robe and gold belt, and made him Promoter of Qinfeng Archer Militia.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and gave him a court robe and gold belt, appointing him promoter of Qinfeng archer militia.

sentences.zh: 時五路並置官，帝謂曰：「卿，吾所親擢也。」

translations.literal: At the time all five circuits simultaneously set up offices; the emperor said to him, "You are one I have personally advanced."
translations.idiomatic: Offices were being set up on all five circuits at once. The emperor told him, "You are a man I promoted myself."

sentences.zh: 貫滋不悅，師道不敢拜，以請，得提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: Guan grew more displeased; Shidao dared not accept the bow; by request he obtained promotion of Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was displeased. Shidao refused the appointment and asked instead to be made promoter of Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，知西安州。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made to know Xi'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became prefect of Xi'anzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏人侵定邊，築佛口城，率師往夷之。

translations.literal: The Xia people raided Dingbian, built Fokou Fort; he led troops to level it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tanguts invaded Dingbian and built Fokou Fort, he led troops to destroy it.

sentences.zh: 始至渴甚，師道指山之西麓曰：「是當有水。」

translations.literal: When first arriving they were extremely thirsty; Shidao pointed to the western slope of the mountain and said, "There ought to be water there."
translations.idiomatic: On arrival his men were parched with thirst. Shidao pointed to the western slope of a mountain and said, "There should be water there."

sentences.zh: 命工求之，果得水滿谷。

translations.literal: He ordered workmen to seek it; indeed they obtained water filling the valley.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers dug and found a spring that filled the valley.

sentences.zh: 累遷龍神衛四廂都指揮使、洺州防禦使、知渭州。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Divine Guard, Defender of Ming Prefecture, and Administrator of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander of the four wings of the Dragon Divine Guard, defender of Mingzhou, and prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 督諸道兵城席葦，土賦工，敵至，堅壁葫蘆河。

translations.literal: He supervised troops of all circuits in walling Xiye; earth was levied for labor; when the enemy came he held walls firm at Hulu River.
translations.idiomatic: He directed troops from every circuit to fortify Xiye, levied labor from the local population, and when the enemy came he held the walls at Hulu River.

sentences.zh: 師道陳於河滸，若將決戰者。

translations.literal: Shidao arrayed at the river bank as if about to join decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao drew up his line on the riverbank as if ready for a decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 陰遣偏將曲克徑出橫嶺，揚言援兵至，敵方駭顧，楊可世潛軍軍其後，姚平仲以精甲衷擊之，敵大潰，斬首五十級，獲橐駝、馬牛萬計，其酋僅以身免。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent flank general Qu Ke straight out over Hengling, proclaiming relief troops had arrived; the enemy in alarm looked about; Yang Keshi secretly stationed troops behind them; Yao Pingzhong with elite armor struck them in the flank; the enemy collapsed greatly; fifty heads were beheaded; camels, horses, and cattle were captured in tens of thousands; their chief barely escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent Qu Ke over Hengling Ridge with word that reinforcements had arrived. While the enemy looked about in alarm, Yang Keshi took troops around their rear and Yao Pingzhong hit them in the flank with elite armor. The enemy broke completely. Fifty heads were taken and tens of thousands of camels, horses, and cattle captured. Their chief barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 卒城而還。

translations.literal: He finished the fort and returned.
