translations.idiomatic: He completed the fort and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又詔帥陝西、河東七路兵征臧底城，期以旬日必克。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to command troops of the seven circuits of Shaanxi and Hedong to campaign against Zangdi Fort, with a deadline of ten days for certain capture.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to lead the seven circuits of Shaanxi and Hedong against Zangdi Fort, with ten days allowed for capture.

sentences.zh: 既薄城下，敵守備甚固。

translations.literal: When already pressing under the walls, the enemy's defense was very solid.
translations.idiomatic: When his army reached the walls, the defense was stubborn.

sentences.zh: 官軍小怠，列校有據胡床自休者，立斬之，屍於軍門。

translations.literal: The official army slackened slightly; a company commander sat on a folding chair resting himself; he was beheaded at once, corpse at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops slackened, he instantly beheaded a company commander found resting on a camp stool and displayed the body at the gate.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「今日城不下，視此。」

translations.literal: His order said, "If today the city is not taken, look to this."
translations.idiomatic: He announced, "If the city is not taken today, you will look like this."

sentences.zh: 眾股栗，噪而登城，城即潰，時兵至才八日。

translations.literal: The crowd's thighs trembled; shouting they mounted the walls; the city at once collapsed; at the time the army had arrived only eight days.
translations.idiomatic: The men shook with fear, stormed the walls with a roar, and the city fell at once—on the eighth day after arrival.

sentences.zh: 帝得捷書喜，進侍衛親軍馬軍副都指揮使、應道軍承宣使。

translations.literal: The emperor received the victory report with joy and advanced him to Deputy Commander of the Palace Guard Horse Army and Commissioner of the Yingdao Army.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted by the victory report, the emperor made him deputy commander of the palace guard horse army and commissioner of the Yingdao army.

sentences.zh: 從童貫為都統制，拜保靜軍節度使。

translations.literal: Following Tong Guan as overall controller, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Tong Guan as overall commander, he was made military commissioner of the Baojing army.

sentences.zh: 貫謀伐燕，使師道盡護諸將。

translations.literal: Guan plotted to campaign against Yan and had Shidao oversee all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Guan planned a campaign against Yan and put Shidao in command of all the generals.

sentences.zh: 師道諫曰：「今日之舉，譬如盜入鄰家不能救，又乘之而分其室焉，無乃不可乎？」

translations.literal: Shidao remonstrated: "Today's action is like a thief entering a neighbor's house whom one cannot save, then taking advantage to divide his rooms—is this not impermissible?"
translations.idiomatic: Shidao warned him: "This campaign is like failing to stop a burglar in a neighbor's house, then rushing in to loot the rooms yourself. Can that be right?"

sentences.zh: 貫不聽。

translations.literal: Guan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Guan refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 既次白溝，遼人噪而前，士卒多傷。

translations.literal: When already encamped at Baigou, the Liao people shouted and advanced; soldiers were many wounded.
translations.idiomatic: At Baigou the Liao charged with a roar and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 師道先令人持一巨梃自防，賴以不大敗。

translations.literal: Shidao first had men hold a huge club for self-defense, and by this was spared a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao had ordered his men to carry huge clubs for self-defense, which helped keep the defeat from becoming a rout.

sentences.zh: 遼使來請曰：「女真之叛本朝，亦南朝之所甚惡也。

translations.literal: A Liao envoy came to plead: "The Jurchens' rebellion against our court is also what the Southern Court greatly detests.
translations.idiomatic: A Liao envoy came and said, "The Jurchens have rebelled against us, and the Song detests them as well.

sentences.zh: 今射一時之利，棄百年之好，結豺狼之鄰，基他日之禍，謂為得計可乎？

translations.literal: Now to shoot at momentary profit, abandon a hundred years' friendship, bind a wolf-and-dog neighbor, lay the foundation of future disaster—can this be called a winning plan?
translations.idiomatic: To seize a moment's advantage, throw away a century of friendship, ally with wolves, and sow tomorrow's disaster—can that be wise?

sentences.zh: 救災恤鄰，古今通義，惟大國圖之。」

translations.literal: Relieving disaster and pitying neighbors is the common principle of ancient and modern times; may the great state consider it."
translations.idiomatic: Aid in disaster and pity for neighbors are eternal principles. Let the great state consider them."

sentences.zh: 貫不能對，師道復諫宜許之，又不聽，密劾其助賊。

translations.literal: Guan could not reply; Shidao again remonstrated that they ought to agree, and again was not heeded; he secretly impeached him for aiding bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Guan had no reply. Shidao urged acceptance again and was ignored again. Guan secretly impeached him for aiding the enemy.

sentences.zh: 王黼怒，責為右衛將軍致仕，而用劉延慶代之。

translations.literal: Wang Fu was angry, demoted him to Right Guard General with retirement, and used Liu Yanqing to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu was furious, forced him to retire as a right guard general, and replaced him with Liu Yanqing.

sentences.zh: 延慶敗績于盧溝，帝思其言，起為憲州刺史、知環州，俄還保靜軍節度使，復致仕。

translations.literal: Yanqing was defeated at Lugou; the emperor recalled his words, restored him as Prefect of Xian Prefecture and Administrator of Huan Prefecture, soon returned him to Military Commissioner of Baojing Army, and again retired him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanqing was defeated at Lugou, the emperor remembered Shidao's warning, recalled him as prefect of Xianzhou and administrator of Huanzhou, soon restored him as military commissioner of Baojing, then retired him again.

sentences.zh: 金人南下，趣召之，加檢校少保、靜難軍節度使、京畿河北制置使，聽便宜檄兵食。

translations.literal: The Jurchens went south; he was urgently summoned, advanced to Acting Junior Guardian, Military Commissioner of Jingnan Army, and Metropolitan Hebei Commissioner, with authority to requisition troops and provisions as expedient.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens marched south he was urgently recalled, made acting junior guardian, military commissioner of Jingnan, and metropolitan Hebei commissioner with authority to levy troops and supplies as needed.

sentences.zh: 師道方居南山豹林谷，聞命即東。

translations.literal: Shidao was just then dwelling in Baolin Valley on South Mountain; hearing the order he at once went east.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was living in retirement at Baolin Valley in the southern hills and marched east as soon as the order came.

sentences.zh: 過姚平仲，有步騎七千，與之俱北。

translations.literal: Passing Yao Pingzhong, he had seven thousand foot and horse, and went north together with him.
translations.idiomatic: He met Yao Pingzhong with seven thousand infantry and cavalry and marched north together.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，聞斡離不已屯京城下，或止勿行曰：「賊勢方銳，願少駐汜水，以謀萬全。」

translations.literal: Reaching Luoyang, he heard Wanyan Zonghan already encamped below the capital; some urged him not to go on, saying, "The bandits' momentum is just sharp—may you briefly halt at Sishui to plan complete security."
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang he learned that Wanyan Zonghan was already below the capital. Some urged him to halt at Sishui while the enemy was still at peak strength.

sentences.zh: 師道曰：「吾兵少，若遲回不進，形見情露，祗取辱焉。

translations.literal: Shidao said, "Our troops are few; if we delay and do not advance, our form is seen and feelings exposed—we only invite disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao said, "We are few. If we hesitate, we reveal our weakness and invite only shame.

sentences.zh: 今鼓行而前，彼安能測我虛實？

translations.literal: Now if we beat drums and advance, how can they measure our emptiness and fullness?
translations.idiomatic: If we march boldly now, how can they tell our true strength?

sentences.zh: 都人知吾來，士氣自振，何憂賊哉！」

translations.literal: When the capital people know we have come, morale will itself be roused—why fear bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Once the capital knows we are coming, morale will rise by itself. What is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 揭榜沿道，言种少保領西兵百萬來。

translations.literal: He posted placards along the road saying Junior Guardian Zhong was leading a million western troops coming.
translations.idiomatic: He posted notices along the road that Junior Guardian Zhong was leading a million western troops.

sentences.zh: 遂抵城西，趨汴水南，徑逼敵營。

translations.literal: He then reached the west of the city, hurried to the south of the Bian River, and directly pressed the enemy camp.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the west of the city, crossed to the south bank of the Bian River, and pressed straight against the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 金人懼，徙砦稍北，斂遊騎，但守牟駝岡，增壘自衛。

translations.literal: The Jurchens were afraid, moved their camp slightly north, gathered in their roaming cavalry, only guarded Mouluo Mound, and added ramparts for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens were alarmed, shifted their camp northward, pulled in their raiders, held only Mouluo Ridge, and threw up extra defenses.

sentences.zh: 時師道春秋高，天下稱為「老种」。

translations.literal: At the time Shidao's spring and autumn were advanced; all under heaven called him "Old Zhong."
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was by then advanced in years, and the empire called him "Old Zhong."

sentences.zh: 欽宗聞其至，喜甚，開安上門，命尚書右丞李綱迎勞。

translations.literal: Qinzong heard he had arrived and was greatly pleased, opened the Anshang Gate, and ordered Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Gang to welcome and console him.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzong was overjoyed at his arrival, opened the Anshang Gate, and sent Vice Director Li Gang to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 時已議和，入見，帝問曰：「今日之事，卿意如何？」

translations.literal: Peace was already under discussion; on entering audience the emperor asked, "Today's affair—what is your thought?"
translations.idiomatic: Peace talks were already under way. At audience the emperor asked, "What do you think of the situation?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「女真不知兵，豈有孤軍深入人境而能善其歸乎？」

translations.literal: He replied, "The Jurchens do not understand warfare—how could a lone army deep in enemy territory make a good return?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The Jurchens know nothing of war. How can a lone army deep in enemy country withdraw safely?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「業已講好矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Peace is already settled."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Peace is already agreed."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣以軍旅之事事陛下，餘非所敢知也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant serves Your Majesty with military affairs; the rest is not what I dare know."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I serve Your Majesty in military matters only. The rest is not for me to say."

sentences.zh: 拜檢校少傅、同知樞密院、京畿兩河宣撫使，諸道兵悉隸焉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Junior Mentor, Associate Military Affairs Commissioner, and Metropolitan Two-He Pacification Commissioner; troops of all circuits were all placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting junior mentor, associate military affairs commissioner, and metropolitan pacification commissioner for the capital region and the two He provinces, with all circuit armies under his command.

sentences.zh: 以平仲為都統制。

translations.literal: Pingzhong was made overall controller.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Pingzhong was made overall commander.

sentences.zh: 師道時被病，命毋拜，許肩輿入朝。

translations.literal: Shidao was then afflicted with illness; he was ordered not to bow and permitted to enter court in a shoulder carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was ill and was excused from bowing and allowed to enter court in a litter.

sentences.zh: 金使王汭在廷頡頏，望見師道，拜跪稍如禮。

translations.literal: The Jin envoy Wang Huan in court was overbearing; seeing Shidao he bowed and knelt somewhat according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin envoy Wang Huan had been insolent in court, but on seeing Shidao he bowed with something like proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 帝顧笑曰：「彼為卿故也。」

translations.literal: The emperor looked back and smiled, saying, "He does this for your sake."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "He does that for your sake."

sentences.zh: 京城自受圍，諸門盡閉，市無薪菜。

translations.literal: Since the capital was besieged all gates were shut and the market had no fuel or vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Since the siege began every gate had been shut and the markets had no fuel or vegetables.

sentences.zh: 師道請啟西、南壁，聽民出入如常。

translations.literal: Shidao requested opening the western and southern walls and allowing the people to go in and out as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao asked that the western and southern gates be opened so people could come and go normally.

sentences.zh: 金人有擅過偏將馬忠軍者，忠斬其六人。

translations.literal: Jurchens who overstepped bounds at flank general Ma Zhong's army—Zhong beheaded six of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jurchens trespassed on the camp of flank general Ma Zhong, Zhong beheaded six of them.

sentences.zh: 金人來訴，師道付以界旗，使自為制，後無有敢越佚者。

translations.literal: The Jurchens came to complain; Shidao gave them border flags and had them regulate themselves; afterward none dared cross or overstep.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens complained, Shidao gave them border flags and told them to police their own men. After that none dared cross the line.

sentences.zh: 又請緩給金幣，使彼惰歸，扼而殲諸河，執政不可。

translations.literal: He also requested delaying payment of gold and coins so they would grow slack in returning, then choke and annihilate them at the river—the chief ministers would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged delaying payment of gold so the enemy would grow careless on the retreat and could be destroyed at the river, but the chief ministers refused.

sentences.zh: 种氏、姚氏皆為山西巨室，平仲父古方以熙河兵入援。

translations.literal: The Zhong and Yao clans were both great houses of Shanxi; Pingzhong's father Gufang had led Xihe troops to enter as relief.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhong and Yao clans were great Shanxi families. Pingzhong's father Gufang had led Xihe troops to the relief army.

sentences.zh: 平仲慮功名獨歸种氏。

translations.literal: Pingzhong feared merit and fame would all return to the Zhong clan.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong feared the Zhong clan alone would win the credit.

sentences.zh: 乃以士不得速戰為言達於上。

translations.literal: He therefore had the words that the army could not fight quickly reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He told the throne that the troops could not be rushed into battle.

sentences.zh: 李綱主其議，令城下兵緩急聽平仲節度。

translations.literal: Li Gang championed his proposal and ordered troops below the walls in urgency or ease to heed Pingzhong's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang backed him and put all troops below the walls under Pingzhong's command.

sentences.zh: 帝日遣使趣師道戰，師道欲俟其弟秦鳳經略使師中至，奏言過春分乃可擊。

translations.literal: The emperor daily sent envoys to urge Shidao to battle; Shidao wished to await his younger brother Qinfeng Frontier Commissioner Shizhong's arrival and memorialized that only after the spring equinox could they strike.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent messengers daily urging Shidao to fight. Shidao wanted to wait for his brother Shizhong, the Qinfeng frontier commissioner, and memorialized that attack should wait until after the spring equinox.

sentences.zh: 時相距才八日，帝以為緩，竟用平仲斫營，以及於敗。

translations.literal: At the time they had faced each other only eight days; the emperor thought this slow and in the end used Pingzhong to storm the camp, thereby reaching defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Only eight days had passed since the armies faced each other. The emperor thought this too slow and finally let Pingzhong storm the enemy camp, which led to defeat.

sentences.zh: 既敗，李邦彥議割三鎮，師道爭之不得。

translations.literal: After defeat Li Bangyan proposed ceding the three prefectures; Shidao contested it but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat Li Bangyan proposed ceding the three prefectures. Shidao objected in vain.

sentences.zh: 李綱罷，太學諸生、都人伏闕願見种、李，詔趣使彈壓。

translations.literal: Li Gang was dismissed; Imperial Academy students and capital people knelt at the palace gate wishing to see Zhong and Li; an edict urgently ordered suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang was dismissed, academy students and capital residents knelt at the palace gate demanding to see Zhong and Li. An edict ordered them suppressed.

sentences.zh: 師道乘車而來，眾褰廉視之，曰：「果我公也。」

translations.literal: Shidao came in a carriage; the crowd lifted the curtain to look at him and said, "It is indeed our lord."
translations.idiomatic: Shidao came in his carriage. The crowd lifted the curtain, looked in, and cried, "It really is our lord."

sentences.zh: 相率聲喏而散。

translations.literal: They followed one another in shouting salute and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: They shouted their salutes one after another and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 金師退，乃罷為中太一宮使。

translations.literal: When the Jin army withdrew, he was dismissed and made Commissioner of the Central Supreme One Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin army withdrew, he was removed from command and made commissioner of the Central Supreme One Palace.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞許翰見帝，以為不宜解師道兵柄。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xu Han saw the emperor and held that Shidao's military authority ought not be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Xu Han told the emperor that Shidao should not be stripped of military command.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「師道老矣，難用，當使卿見之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Shidao is old and hard to employ—you should be made to see him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shidao is old and hard to use. I will have you meet him."

sentences.zh: 令相見於殿門外。

translations.literal: He ordered them to meet outside the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: He had them meet outside the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 師道不語，翰曰：「國家有急，詔許訪所疑，公勿以書生之故不肯談。」

translations.literal: Shidao did not speak; Han said, "The state has urgency; an edict permits inquiry into doubts—my lord, do not because of being a scholar refuse to discuss."
translations.idiomatic: Shidao said nothing. Han said, "The state is in crisis and the edict allows us to consult you. Do not refuse to speak because you are a scholar."

sentences.zh: 師道始言：「我眾彼寡，但分兵結營，控守要地，使彼糧道不通，坐以持久，可破也。」

translations.literal: Shidao then first spoke: "We are many and they few—only divide troops and establish camps, hold strategic points, cut off their grain routes, and sit in endurance; they can be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Shidao finally spoke: "We outnumber them. Divide the army into camps, hold the key passes, cut their supply lines, and wear them down—they can be defeated."

sentences.zh: 翰歎味其言，復上奏謂師道智慮未衰，尚可用。

translations.literal: Han sighed and savored his words, again memorialized that Shidao's wisdom and counsel had not declined and could still be used.
translations.idiomatic: Han marveled at his words and memorialized again that Shidao's mind was still sharp and he should be kept in service.

sentences.zh: 於是加檢校少師，進太尉，換節鎮洮軍，為河北、河東宣撫使，屯滑州，實無兵自隨。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was advanced to Acting Junior Mentor, promoted to Grand Marshal, exchanged his commission to command the Tao Army, made Hebei and Hedong Pacification Commissioner, encamped at Hua Prefecture, but in truth had no troops following him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting junior mentor and grand marshal, given command of the Tao army, appointed pacification commissioner of Hebei and Hedong, and posted at Huazhou—but in truth he had no troops with him.

sentences.zh: 師道請合關、河卒屯滄、衛、孟、滑，備金兵再至。

translations.literal: Shidao requested combining Guan and He troops to encamp at Cang, Wei, Meng, and Hua to prepare for the Jin army coming again.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao asked to concentrate Guan and He troops at Cang, Wei, Meng, and Hua in case the Jin returned.

sentences.zh: 朝論以大敵甫退，不宜勞師以示弱，格不用。

translations.literal: Court opinion held that with the great enemy just withdrawn, one ought not weary the army to show weakness; it was blocked and not used.
translations.idiomatic: The court argued that with the great enemy just gone, massing troops would look weak, and rejected the plan.

sentences.zh: 既而師中戰死，姚古敗，朝廷震悚，召師道還。

translations.literal: Presently Shizhong died in battle, Yao Gu was defeated, the court was shaken and alarmed, and Shidao was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shizhong was killed in battle and Yao Gu was defeated. The court was shaken and recalled Shidao.

sentences.zh: 太原陷，又使巡邊。

translations.literal: Taiyuan fell, and he was again sent to tour the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan fell he was sent to inspect the frontier again.

sentences.zh: 次河陽，遇王汭，揣敵必大舉，亟上疏請幸長安以避其鋒。

translations.literal: Halting at Heyang, he met Wang Huan, guessed the enemy would certainly make a great effort, and urgently memorialized requesting the emperor visit Chang'an to avoid their edge.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyang he met Wang Huan, judged that the enemy would strike in force, and urgently memorialized for the emperor to move to Chang'an to avoid their blow.

sentences.zh: 大臣以為怯，復召還。

translations.literal: The chief ministers thought this cowardly and summoned him back again.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers called this cowardice and recalled him again.

sentences.zh: 既至，病不能見。

translations.literal: When he had arrived, he was ill and could not be received.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he was too ill to appear at court.

sentences.zh: 十月，卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he died at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 帝臨奠，哭之慟，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to offer sacrifice, wept for him bitterly, and posthumously granted Grand Preceptor with Insignia Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn him, wept bitterly, and posthumously granted him grand preceptor with insignia equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 京師失守，帝搏膺曰：「不用种師道言，以至於此！」

translations.literal: When the capital was lost the emperor beat his breast and said, "For not using Zhong Shidao's words we have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell the emperor beat his breast and cried, "Because we did not heed Zhong Shidao, we have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 金兵之始退也，師道申前議，勸帝乘半濟擊之，不從，曰：「異日必為國患。」

translations.literal: When the Jin troops first withdrew, Shidao repeated his former proposal, urging the emperor to strike them while half across the river; he was not heeded, and said, "Another day they will surely be the state's calamity."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin first withdrew, Shidao renewed his old proposal to strike them mid-crossing. The court refused. He said, "They will be a national disaster yet."

sentences.zh: 故追痛其語。

translations.literal: Therefore he painfully recalled his words.
translations.idiomatic: That is why he mourned those words afterward.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，加贈少保，諡曰「忠憲」。

translations.literal: In the Jianyan era he was further posthumously granted Junior Guardian, posthumous title "Loyal and Lawful."
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianyan era he was further posthumously made junior guardian with the posthumous title Loyal and Lawful.

sentences.zh: 孫 師中

translations.literal: Grandson: Shizhong
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Shizhong

sentences.zh: 師中，字端孺。

translations.literal: Shizhong, styled Duanru.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong, whose courtesy name was Duanru.

sentences.zh: 歷知環、濱、邠州、慶陽府、秦州，侍衛步軍馬軍副都指揮使、房州觀察使，奉寧軍承宣使。

translations.literal: He successively administered Huan, Bin, Bin, Qingyang Prefecture, and Qin Prefecture; was Deputy Commander of the Palace Guard Foot and Horse Armies; Observation Commissioner of Fang Prefecture; and Commissioner of the Fengning Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Huan, Bin, and Qin, administrator of Qingyang, deputy commander of the palace guard foot and horse armies, observation commissioner of Fangzhou, and commissioner of the Fengning army.

sentences.zh: 金人內侵，詔提秦鳳兵入援，未至而敵退，乃以二萬人守滑。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded within, an edict ordered him to lead Qinfeng troops in relief; before arriving the enemy withdrew, and he then used twenty thousand to guard Hua.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded, he was ordered to lead Qinfeng troops to the relief army. Before he arrived the enemy withdrew, and he kept twenty thousand men at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 遣副姚古為河北制置使，古援太原，師中援中山、河間。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Gu as deputy Hebei Commissioner; Gu relieved Taiyuan, Shizhong relieved Zhongshan and Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yao Gu as Hebei commissioner to relieve Taiyuan while he himself moved to relieve Zhongshan and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 或謂師中自磁、相而北，金人若下太行，則勢不能自還，此段凝師於河上比也。

translations.literal: Some said if Shizhong went north from Ci and Xiang, and the Jurchens came down the Taihang, he could not by momentum return himself—this was like Duan Ning's freezing the army on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that if Shizhong marched north from Ci and Xiang while the Jurchens came down the Taihang range, he could not get back—just as Duan Ning had once trapped his army on the river.

sentences.zh: 時大臣立議矛盾，樞密主破敵，而三省令護出之。

translations.literal: At the time the chief ministers' established proposals contradicted; the Military Affairs Bureau championed destroying the enemy, while the Three Departments ordered protecting the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion was divided: the Bureau of Military Affairs wanted to destroy the enemy, while the Three Departments ordered a cautious advance.

sentences.zh: 師中渡河，即上言：「粘罕已至澤州，臣欲由邢、相間捷出上黨，搗其不意，當可以逞。」

translations.literal: Shizhong crossed the river and at once submitted: "Wanyan Zonghan has already reached Ze Prefecture; your servant wishes by a swift route between Xing and Xiang to emerge on Shangdang and strike their unpreparedness—it should succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong crossed the river and memorialized at once: "Wanyan Zonghan has reached Zezhou. I wish to strike out through Xing and Xiang into Shangdang and hit them unprepared."

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑不用。

translations.literal: The court was doubtful and did not use it.
translations.idiomatic: The court hesitated and did not approve.

sentences.zh: 斡離不還，師中逐出境。

translations.literal: Wanyan Zonghan returned, and Shizhong drove him beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanyan Zonghan withdrew, Shizhong pursued him beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 粘罕至太原，悉破諸縣，為鎖城法困之，內外不相通。

translations.literal: Zonghan reached Taiyuan, broke all the counties, used the chained-city method to besiege it, and inner and outer did not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan reached Taiyuan, overran the surrounding counties, and besieged the city with chained forts so that nothing could get in or out.

sentences.zh: 姚古雖復隆德、威勝，扼南北關，而不能解圍。

translations.literal: Though Yao Gu recovered Longde and Weisheng and choked the north and south passes, he could not lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Gu recovered Longde and Weisheng and held the north and south passes, but could not break the siege.

sentences.zh: 於是詔師中由井陘道出師，與古掎角，進次平定軍，乘勝復壽陽、榆次，留屯真定。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Shizhong to take troops out by the Jingxing route, coordinate with Gu in pincer, advance to station at Pingding Army, on momentum recover Shouyang and Yuci, and remain encamped at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Shizhong out by the Jingxing route to coordinate with Gu in a pincer. He advanced to Pingding, recovered Shouyang and Yuci on the momentum of victory, and encamped at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 時粘罕避暑雲中，留兵分就畜牧，覘者以為將遁，告諸朝。

translations.literal: At the time Zonghan summered in Yunzhong, left troops dispersed to pasture; scouts thought he would flee and reported to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan was summering in Yunzhong and had dispersed his men to pasture their herds. Scouts thought he was about to flee and so reported to court.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院許翰信之，數遣使督師中出戰，且責以逗撓。

translations.literal: Military Affairs Commissioner Xu Han believed it, repeatedly sent envoys to urge Shizhong to battle, and moreover blamed him for delay and hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs commissioner Xu Han believed them and repeatedly ordered Shizhong into battle, accusing him of delay.

sentences.zh: 師中歎曰：「逗撓，兵家大戮也。

translations.literal: Shizhong sighed and said, "Delay and hesitation are the great punishment in warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong sighed and said, "Delay is the gravest military crime.

sentences.zh: 吾結髮從軍，今老矣，忍受此為罪乎！」

translations.literal: I have bound my hair and followed the army; now I am old—can I bear to accept this as crime!"
translations.idiomatic: I have been a soldier since youth. I am old now—how can I bear to die under that charge?"

sentences.zh: 即日辦嚴，約古及張灝俱進，輜重賞犒之物，皆不暇從行。

translations.literal: That very day he prepared in earnest, arranged with Gu and Zhang Hao to advance together; baggage, rewards, and consolation goods—all had no leisure to follow.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he made ready to march, arranged with Gu and Zhang Hao to advance together, and had no time even to bring supplies and rewards.

sentences.zh: 五月，抵壽陽之石坑，為金人所襲。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he reached Shiyang's Stone Pit and was attacked by the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he reached the Stone Pit near Shouyang and was ambushed by the Jin.

sentences.zh: 五戰三勝，回趨榆次，去太原百里，而古、灝失期不至，兵饑甚。

translations.literal: In five battles three victories; turning back toward Yuci, a hundred li from Taiyuan, yet Gu and Hao missed the date and did not arrive; the troops were very hungry.
translations.idiomatic: In five engagements he won three, then turned toward Yuci a hundred li from Taiyuan. Gu and Hao failed to rendezvous, and his men were starving.

sentences.zh: 敵知之，悉眾攻，右軍潰而前軍亦奔。

translations.literal: The enemy knew it, attacked with all their forces; the right wing collapsed and the front army also fled.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy learned of their weakness and attacked in full force. The right wing broke and the van fled as well.

sentences.zh: 師中獨以麾下死戰，自卯至巳，士卒發神臂弓射退金兵，而賞齎不及，皆憤怨散去，所留者才百人。

translations.literal: Shizhong alone with his followers fought to the death from the mao hour to the si hour; soldiers shot with divine-arm bows and drove back the Jin troops, but rewards did not reach them and all resentfully dispersed in anger; those who remained were only a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong alone fought on with his personal guard from dawn until mid-morning. His men used divine-arm bows to drive the Jin back, but rewards never came and they dispersed in anger. Only a hundred remained.

sentences.zh: 師中身被四創，力疾鬪死。

translations.literal: Shizhong's body received four wounds; exerting his strength in illness he fought and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong took four wounds and fought on through his illness until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 師中老成持重，為時名將，諸軍自是氣奪。

translations.literal: Shizhong was mature, steady, and weighty, a famed general of the age; from this all armies had their spirit seized.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong had been a seasoned, respected general of his day, and after his death the armies lost heart.

sentences.zh: 劉韐言：「師中聞命即行，奮不顧身，雖古忠臣，不過也。」

translations.literal: Liu Yan said, "Shizhong on hearing orders at once went forth, striving without regard for body—even ancient loyal ministers did not surpass this."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan said, "Shizhong marched the moment he was ordered and gave his life without hesitation—even the loyal ministers of antiquity did no more."

sentences.zh: 請加優贈，以勸死國者。

translations.literal: He requested added generous posthumous grant to encourage those who die for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a generous posthumous reward to encourage others to die for the state.

sentences.zh: 詔贈少師，諡曰「莊湣」。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Junior Guardian, posthumous title "Solemn and Sorrowful."
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him junior guardian with the posthumous title Solemn and Sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋懲五季藩鎮之弊，稍用逢掖治邊陲、領介胄。

translations.literal: The critique says: Song punished the abuses of the Five Dynasties' frontier commands and slightly used scholars in robes to govern borderlands and lead armor.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: The Song, wary of the Five Dynasties' warlord abuses, increasingly put robed scholars in charge of the frontier and the command of armies.

sentences.zh: 然兵勢國之大事，非素明習，而欲應變決策於急遽危難之際，豈不僕哉。

translations.literal: Yet military momentum is a great affair of state; without long familiarity and practice, yet wishing to respond to change and decide policy in moments of urgent peril and difficulty—how is this not stumbling?
translations.idiomatic: Yet military power is a matter of national survival. Men untrained in war cannot be expected to make sound decisions in sudden crisis without stumbling.

sentences.zh: 种氏自世衡立功青澗，撫循士卒，威動羌、夏，諸子俱有將材，至師道、師中已三世，號山西名將。

translations.literal: The Zhong clan from Shiheng's merit at Qingjian, cherishing and guiding troops, awe moving Qiang and Xia—all sons had general's talent; reaching Shidao and Shizhong it was already three generations, styled famous generals of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: From Shiheng's service at Qingjian the Zhong clan won the loyalty of their soldiers and awed the Qiang and Tanguts. His sons all showed generalship, and by the time of Shidao and Shizhong—three generations—they were called the great generals of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 徽宗任宦豎起邊釁，師道之言不售，卒基南北之禍。

translations.literal: Huizong employed eunuch minions to raise border incidents; Shidao's words were not sold, and in the end laid the foundation of north-south calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong trusted eunuch favorites who stirred border trouble. Shidao's counsel went unheeded, and the catastrophe between north and south was laid.

sentences.zh: 金以孤軍深入，師道請遲西師之至而擊之，長驅上黨；

translations.literal: The Jin with a lone army deep within, Shidao requested delaying until the western army arrived to strike them, and a long drive into Shangdang;
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin drove deep with a lone army, Shidao urged waiting for the western forces and striking them mid-crossing, or sweeping into Shangdang;

sentences.zh: 師中欲出其背以掩之，可謂至計矣。

translations.literal: Shizhong wished to emerge behind them to cover and strike—this may be called the utmost plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong wanted to take them from the rear—a plan of the highest order.

sentences.zh: 李綱、許翰顧以為怯緩逗撓，動失機會，遂至大衄，而國隨以敗，惜哉！

translations.literal: Li Gang and Xu Han instead thought it cowardly, slow, and delaying, constantly missing opportunity, thereby reaching great defeat, and the state followed in collapse—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Gang and Xu Han called such counsel cowardly delay, missed chance after chance, brought on great defeat, and the state fell with it. Alas!
